meta.method: static RE only; nothing here has been confirmed in-game

report.summary:
All VAs are from the 2026-11-02 AceCombat8.exe (551,201,904 bytes, base 0x140000000). Evidence dumps are in <scratchpad>/pvp_research/deep-outside/.

1. Only three Strix SDK success callbacks set ULiveStrixManager+0x1fa: CreateRoomSuccess 0x1474ee290, JoinRoomSuccess 0x1474ee2f0 and JoinNodeRoomSuccess 0x1474ee380. The last one also sets +0x1f9. All three bind the Strix relay first. +0x1f9 gates the network-manager tick's room-supervision block. With a null Strix client that block clears both flags and leaves the room with "room server connection close". So a stand-in must never set +0x1f9.
2. +0x1fa is read at 128 sites in 101 functions. Every Live read of the Strix client global 0x14e4c5818 is null-checked, and the one send path 0x1474a2190 drops messages when the global is null.
3. With +0x1fa=0 the game sends nothing to Strix. Even with +0x1fa=1 and the global null, nothing reaches Strix; what changes is the local logic: both PCs become host with member id 0, timeouts are armed, damage waits for server results, and the game stops scoring.
4. ULiveNetworkP2P (GI+0x930) is not a gameplay seam. It is an EOS P2P transport on socket "INVITE_PAETY" that carries only party-invite strings. It is started by EOS-login and online-entry callbacks, and deathmatch never uses it.
5. The online-only outside channels I found, other than Strix, are:
   - the Chronicle matchmaker (GI+0x918, a UChronicleMatchmakerClient);
   - the Strix Messenger (GI+0x920, null-guarded on MessengerClient +0xf8);
   - the Bandai web API through LiveWebAPI_ (GI+0x970), gated by 0x147926ce0 and 0x147959480;
   - EOS (P2P, plus voice, lobbies and anti-cheat, which are reached only from plugin code).
6. The game's own anti-cheat touchpoints are callbacks of the EOS anti-cheat client: 0x147483e30 sends peer data, 0x147484230 reports an EAC kick, 0x147483fb0 handles a self-kick and 0x1474842e0 handles an integrity violation. ULiveAntiCheatManager (GI+0x988) binds them at GI init. They never fire while that client is absent.
7. The game also has its own network cheat checks: weapon id, damage, ammo, cooltime, player location and combat zone, all reporting into ReportCheat 0x1474b8bb0.
8. Important: the combat-zone check in plane code 0x147d5af30 runs in a deathmatch even offline. It is gated by 0x147ec94e0, which calls DM vslot +0xa10, and that slot is a plain return-true.
9. With the flag set, ReportCheat also records into NetworkCheatManager+0x88. OnGameFinish then hands those records to the cheat-report web call at 0x1474a3830 -> 0x1479b3e60. The game additionally keeps abuse types in a save field (ULiveAccountSaveGame.CheatRecordList +0x430) that the matchmaker's lobby-join arguments include (AbuseTypes).
10. Recommendation: use the offline-host model (+0x1fa = +0x1f9 = 0 on both PCs), with RVNG calling the few online pieces it needs directly. Add three safety detours: make ReportCheat a no-op, and force the two LiveWebAPI gates to return false. Do not flip the flag globally. The local stand-in model needs at least 12 detours and has to re-implement the server's damage, score and end-of-match rules. It also puts the cheat-report and web-API paths one session token away from Bandai.

findings.topic: Writers of StrixManager +0x1fa / +0x1f9 / +0x1f8 / +0x30
findings.finding: Constructor 0x1474ec410 zeroes +0x1f8 (word) and +0x1fa. CreateRoomSuccess 0x1474ee290 calls the relay bind 0x1474eee50 and then sets +0x1fa=1 at 0x1474ee2ab. JoinRoomSuccess 0x1474ee2f0 binds 0x1474eee50 when +0x30==0 and 0x1474ee670 otherwise, then sets +0x1fa=1 at 0x1474ee326 and calls 0x1474ede60. JoinNodeRoomSuccess 0x1474ee380 binds 0x1474eee50 and writes word 0x0101 to +0x1f9 at 0x1474ee39b, which sets both +0x1f9 and +0x1fa. All three are handlers bound in StrixManager init 0x1474ec7e0, so only the Strix SDK fires them. Clearers: the NM tick at 0x1474ad748 (word +0x1f9=0, so +0x1fa is cleared too) and Leave 0x1474b5650 (+0x30=0xff at 0x1474b571d; +0x1f9 word and +0x1f8 set to 0). +0x30 (room kind) is written only from NM+0x3a8 in JoinRoomByMatchedInfo 0x1474b6bc0 (0x1474b6e1d) and by Leave. The NM tick clears +0x1f8 (master-server connected) when the global is null or global+0xe0==0 (0x1474ad5ff-0x1474ad615).

findings.topic: +0x1f9 room-supervision block in the NM tick 0x1474ad560
findings.finding: 0x1474ad634 skips 0x1474ad641-0x1474add9e when +0x1f9==0. If +0x1f9 is set, the block checks that StrixLibrary (+0x28) is valid, that the global is non-null and that the channel-map entry (global+0x50, key NM+0x520) passes 0x14a44c700. If any check fails it clears word +0x1f9 and then logs 'ULiveNetworkManager::Tick : room server connection close', calling LeaveRoom 0x1474b5650 and showing an error (variants: Disconnected from the room server, Load timeout, Return to title upon sleep disconnection). When +0x1fa is also set and member count 0x1474b39e0 is 0, it logs 'number of room member is 0' and leaves the room. The block also has a 'received message was too old' check. After the block: +0x1f9 && +0x1fa -> 0x1474bb230. Timeouts 0x1474b94f0 and 0x1474ba7d0 always run. Every 60 s, if NM+0x5e0 && +0x1fa && NM+0x4c0, a LatencyCheck is sent through 0x1474ceb60 (null-guarded send). Conclusion: with a null Strix client, +0x1f9=1 kicks the player out on the first tick; +0x1fa alone with +0x1f9=0 never enters the block.

findings.topic: +0x1fa readers by subsystem (128 sites, 101 functions; +0x1f9 only in NM tick, timeouts, leave and JoinNodeRoomSuccess)
findings.finding: State machine: NextState 0x1471c6150, TeleportPlayers 0x1471c6c90 and PhaseState 0x1471b9810 use member index 0x1474efb30 and the NM+0x210 member table, and send through the system object. Wait bookkeeping (NM+0x718 bits, NM+0x710 time) is set in TimeSync, SpawnAIs, the IGC waits, SyncStartMatch, GameTerminating and SyncEvaluation. Online-armed timers: SyncStartMatch Enter -> NM+0x620; slot +0x9f8 0x1471c5180 -> NM+0x61c NPC lottery (also writes NM+0x739=0 unconditionally at 0x1471c5242); PreparingMissionEnd 0x1471cb5e0 -> NM+0x624; 0x1474ae5e0 -> NM+0x630 phase sync. Gates: SyncStartMatch Tick 0x1471c7a70; SpawnAIs Tick 0x1471c6a72 (online waits on 0x147ecd400()+0x31). Network objects: local spawn 0x1471b66a0 (role 3 if online, else 1); 0x1471bd590/0x1471bdec0 (role, count); owner migration 0x1471b7840; AI 0x147df8c90; game-object setup 0x147d13e7c / 0x147c853dc (vslots +0xc60/+0xc58/+0xc68); GM network object 0x1471b5920 (vf+0xc48/+0xc50, id 6<<56). Damage/score: TakeDamage 0x147d1037d (report-only), score gate 0x147d10ea1. Cheat: ReportCheat 0x1474b8bb0, CheatMgr vote 0x1474a3430. NM core: host test 0x1474b38d0, member count 0x1474b39e0. Members/MRMM: 0x1474845d0, 0x147491990 (web API through UDM+0xfb0). HUD/lobby/result: about 30 functions, for example 0x14818a6d0 (returns +0x1fa as an IsOnline flag for UI), ALiveResultAvatarGameMode 0x1480f1e50/0x1480f3de0, and 0x14813a280..0x14813ab60 (send when +0x30 is 1 or 2). Faction: only FreeFlight 0x1471b3a00/0x1471b37f0; the DM assigner 0x1471e0230 never reads +0x1fa.

findings.topic: NM timeout supervisor 0x1474b94f0 (called every tick)
findings.finding:
Timers and their error strings, all passed to the error/leave helper 0x1474b9d80:
- NM+0x610: 'aircraft select room connect fail'
- +0x1f9 test at 0x1474b9630: 'room server connect timeout'
- +0x1fa==0 at 0x1474b96d3 with OnJoinRoomComplete 0x1474b83d0(fail): 'room join timeout'
- 'not all users joined timeout'
- NM+0x614: 'aircraft information recv timeout' (also calls MRMM 0x14748e3c0)
- NM+0x61c: 'Random lottery timeout'
- NM+0x620: 'mission start timeout'; reads +0x1fa at 0x1474b9a8c/0x1474b9aa2 and phaseIndex 0x1471c1050
- NM+0x624: 'reward retrieval timeout'; reads +0x1fa at 0x1474b9bb6 together with GM+0x80c/+0x804
- NM+0x628 and NM+0x630: phase-state sync
Offline the timers are never armed. Under a stand-in model every one of them is armed by the online states and fires unless RVNG answers or disarms it.

findings.topic: Strix client global 0x14e4c5818: who creates and clears it
findings.finding:
The only writer is 0x1452935d0 (store at 0x1452936ca). It is reached from:
- the StrixSDK Blueprint exec thunks InitializeStrixNetwork 0x1451eb590 -> 0x1452390d0 -> 0x1452935d0, and InitializeStrixNetworkWithHttpAccessToken 0x1451eb770 -> 0x14528c6a0 -> 0x1452935d0 (native table 0x14bfabff0/0x14bfac000);
- Live: ULiveStrixManager init 0x1474ec7e0 -> 0x1452390d0, called only from 0x1477f9850 (functor 0x14781d890, vtable 0x14cba1298, the online-entry flow; 0x1477f9850 also starts the messenger 0x1474f0200).
Cleared by 0x1452939f0, reached from StopStrixNetwork 0x1451f6f40, from 0x14528c9e0 (vtable slot 0x14bfbae20) and from Live 0x1474ed7e0 <- 'Return To Title' 0x147eca510. In Survival / offline play nothing calls these, so the global stays null (inferred from callers; not checked at runtime).

findings.topic: Live -> Strix SDK / Strix plugin calls and their null behaviour
findings.finding:
Direct SDK calls (0x14a4xxxxx):
- send 0x14a4379a0, only from 0x1474a2190; member-targeted send 0x14a4371a0, only from 0x1474a2560 <- 0x1474a2300 <- lobby UI 0x14813e610. Both test the global and return quietly when it is null.
- relay binding 0x14a434fc0/0x14a435e40/0x14a49ad30..0x14a49b120, from 0x1474eee50/0x1474ee670, reached only from the room-success handlers.
- 0x14a4a1750..0x14a4a1830 from the relay lambdas 0x14750c740..0x14750cc00 (run only when relay messages arrive).
- 0x14a44c700 in the NM tick, inside the +0x1f9 block, after a null test.
- messenger SDK pump 0x14a3c06f0 from the GI tick 0x1478cccd0, only when messenger+0xb0 is non-null.
Plugin wrappers, all behind a null test of the global in the Live caller:
- member id 0x1474efb30 -> 0x1452947b0 (returns 0 when null); first member 0x1474efc20 -> 0x145294cc0 (returns 0); count 0x1474b39e0 (0 when offline or null)
- room property 0x1474ed840 -> 0x1452945a0 (sets *found=0)
- sync time 0x14528cb50 from 0x1471c6230 and 0x1474b3930
- 0x145239ab0 from system-object handler 0x1474cdb90
- 0x1452392f0/0x145239880 from leave 0x1474b5650/0x1474b5820; 0x145249ab0 from 0x1474b77e0; 0x145290450 from 0x1474b7c10; 0x145291ca0 from 0x1474ede60
The prior attempt listed 30 Live readers of the global; all branch on null. The 0x1452adxxx-0x1452b7xxx calls are FLiveMessage type getters and serializers and make no network call. The StrixManager tick 0x1474efd50 only walks the +0x2e0 id map and runs 0x1474a2770 per object locally.

findings.topic: GI per-frame online pump 0x1478cccd0 (bound from GI init 0x1478c9a80)
findings.finding:
Each frame, with each step guarded by its own null test:
- [GI+0x910] StrixManager tick 0x1474efd50
- [GI+0x920] messenger: if +0xb0, the Strix Messenger SDK 0x14a3c06f0
- [GI+0x928] NM tick 0x1474ad560
- [GI+0x930] NetworkP2P: if +0x28 (initialised), ReceivePacket 0x1474c16b0
- [GI+0x948] PartyManager tick 0x1474dcec0
- later [GI+0x9f8] 0x1474d2ae0 and [GI+0xa00] 0x1474d1ad0
The NM system object NM+0x4c0 is created at GI init 0x1474acd50 (called at 0x1478ca4ef), so it exists offline too. Offline sends are therefore stopped only by the null global inside 0x1474a2190.

findings.topic: ULiveNetworkP2P (GI+0x930): an EOS P2P party-invite transport
findings.finding:
Methods:
- Init 0x1474c0a70: gets the online subsystem through 0x1450a8020(0x14e2fad68) and its vf+0x218 platform handle into the global 0x14e50fda8, then calls 0x1474c0e00.
- 0x1474c0e00: EOS_Platform_GetP2PInterface, EOS_P2P_QueryNATType, AddNotifyPeerConnectionRequest and AddNotifyPeerConnectionEstablished on socket 'INVITE_PAETY', SetRelayControl; sets this+0x28=1.
- Shutdown 0x1474c1160; SendPacket 0x1474c11d0 (reliable/unreliable modes); ReceivePacket and dispatch 0x1474c16b0 (only 'RequestInviteToParty:' and 'RequestAcceptInvite:'); connection request -> AcceptConnection 0x1474c21f0; established 0x1474c23f0.
- Local ProductUserId 0x1474c0d10: when null, send and receive do nothing.
Users:
- init from EOS login-state functors 0x14749e9d0/0x14749eaa0 (vtables 0x14cb63d20/0x14cb63d18) and from the online-entry functor 0x1477f7160
- party invite 0x1474e5810 (PARTY_REQUEST_INVITE_TO_PARTY) -> 0x1474c2520 -> send, called from the Result GM 0x1480ecce0 (0x1480ed786) when a party exists
- accept 0x1474c2a20 <- functor 0x1474e9c20
- shutdowns 0x1474d89c0, 0x147b395d0, 0x147eca440
No game-mode state, plane, damage or score code touches it, so the online deathmatch does not use it. RVNG must not reuse it either: it would put EOS traffic on the wire.

findings.topic: EOS and Steam entry points
findings.finding: EOSSDK-Win64-Shipping.dll and steam_api64.dll are both delay-loaded (EOS IAT 0x14de73ea8..0x14de744xx). Live-module code calls EOS directly in only two places: the ULiveNetworkP2P functions (P2P_* and Platform_GetP2PInterface) and EOS_Platform_GetNetworkStatus in 0x14795b400. All other EOS calls are in plugin code: Platform_Create in the virtual 0x14513c340 (vtables 0x14bf9f0c8/0x14bf9f440), Auth/Connect login 0x1451a9970..0x1451ac270, Lobby/Sessions 0x145175120..0x14518f6a0, RTC voice 0x145144900..0x145154080, Ecom, Player/TitleStorage, Stats. The EOS_AntiCheatClient_* wrappers are slots 0x14bfa6ac0..0x14bfa6af0 of a vtable whose constructor 0x1543c0100 is in the protected .sbss section (not analysed). Steam: Live calls SteamAPI_Init (0x14798e560, 0x14808f4f0) and interface accessors (SteamUtils 0x1475134c0, SteamApps 0x1478ff4e0, SteamFriends 0x14791e260). SteamNetworking006 and SteamMatchMaking009 are used only by the OnlineSubsystemSteam plugin (0x1481ddba0/0x1481ddbd0/0x1481ddae0). None of these is on the deathmatch path.

findings.topic: Chronicle matchmaker, Strix Messenger, LiveWebAPI
findings.finding: MatchmakerManager_ (GI+0x918, TMap MatchmakerClientControllerMap +0x118; controller -> UChronicleMatchmakerClient +0x40; Init(Url, WebUrl, MasterServerUrls) and heartbeat) is used only in the lobby/matchmaking flow: 0x1474ae300, 0x1474af750, 0x1474b1e60 (OnMatchmakerMatched), JoinRoomByMatchedInfo 0x1474b6bc0, 0x147eca510. StrixMessenger_ (GI+0x920, UStrixMessengerClient at +0xf8): subscribe paths such as 0x1474f16d0 (SubscribeLobbyTopic) and 0x1474f0b60 test +0xf8 for null. The Result GM 0x1480ecce0 calls messenger 0x1474f16d0/0x1474f0b60 and party code. Web API: requests go through UDM+0xfb0 (0x147957eb0/0x147957450, gate 0x147959480) or the UDM+0x12a0 object (0x1479b3e60, gate 0x147926ce0). Both gates cache GI+0x970 LiveWebAPI_ and fail when the API object or session (+0x30/+0x108/+0x110) is missing.

findings.topic: Anti-cheat manager and EAC callbacks (game side only)
findings.finding:
ULiveAntiCheatManager is GI+0x988 (getter 0x147eced00). Its init 0x147483390 runs from GI init 0x1478c9a80. It gets an interface through 0x1450a8020 and returns at once when that is null (0x1474833cf). Otherwise it binds:
- vf+0x90 -> 0x147483e30: message to peer -> 0x1474b9ee0 -> 0x1474ce9d0 -> Strix send of FLiveMessageEasyAntiCheatPeerData
- vf+0x98 -> 0x147483fb0: 'OnAntiCheatSelfKicked' -> LeaveRoom 0x1474b5650 + error
- vf+0xa0 -> 0x147484230: ReportCheat(type 1 client_eac_kick)
- vf+0xa8 -> 0x1474842e0: 'Anti cheat client Integrity violated' error
- other delegates 0x147484ef0/0x147485020/0x147485050
A second peer-data sender, 0x1474845d0, is reached through functor 0x14749ef70. The receive handler 0x1474d0970 (system object) -> 0x1474b9ff0 reads the member 'userid' and passes the data to the anti-cheat client. The Result GM (0x1480eceff) calls 0x147485660 only when AntiCheatManager+0x28 is non-null; 0x147485660 issues a UDM+0xfb0 web request. 'Restrictions by easy anti cheat' with CancelMatch (0x1474af800, from matchmaking UI 0x14756f8f0/0x1477e77d0) and RESTRICT_MATCHMAKING / RESTRICT_GAME_ACCESS (0x147485350) are lobby-side only. With no anti-cheat client (modded, -eac-nop-loaded) none of these fire. If one did, its Strix send would drop on the null global.

findings.topic: Game-side network cheat checks, ReportCheat 0x1474b8bb0 and the cheat vote
findings.finding:
ELiveNetworkCheatType values: 1 eac_kick, 2 npc_location, 3 player_location, 4 damage, 5 weapon_cooltime, 6 weapon_ammo, 7 weapon_id, 8 weapon_location, 9 combat_zone. Callers and the types they report:
- 0x1474a3cb0, inside ApplyNetworkDamage 0x1474aacb0: types 7 and 4; it rejects implausible DamageClient values using 0x147d41a20
- 0x1474a3f20 <- 0x1474aa1c0: type 3
- 0x1474a41a0: types 6 and 5
- player-plane handlers 0x1474c73f0/0x1474c76c0/0x1474c79b0: type 5
- plane 0x147d5af30: type 9
- 0x147484230: type 1
ReportCheat does three things:
1. sends a Cheat message through the system object 0x1474cecc0 -> 0x1474a2190 (dropped when the global is null);
2. calls the NetworkCheatManager (GI+0x938) vote 0x1474a3430 through 0x1474b8de0;
3. only if (NM+0x4c9 || +0x1fa) && +0x30==0, records the type in MRMM 0x147492510 and in NetworkCheatManager+0x88.
The vote kicks only when +0x1fa is set, the channel is connected (0x1474b3860) and the vote is a majority: 'Kick Room Member' -> 0x1474b5820 when the accused is self, otherwise a KickPlayer send 0x1474cee50. Offline or with a null global it only records votes.
sources: gctx.py r8b at ReportCheat sites (this session)

findings.topic: Combat-zone check runs in a deathmatch even offline
findings.finding: 0x147d5af30 (reached from 0x147d45a52) calls 0x147ec94e0(world). For the online GM class (0x146dcdcf0) that function returns AuthorityGameMode vf+0xa10. DM vtable 0x14c693718 slot +0xa10 is 0x1416bb960 (mov al,1; ret). The check then needs DM vf+0xb70 (GM+0x520 byte) and plane+0x1309. While the plane is outside the zone box it adds up time, and past the threshold it calls ReportCheat(NM, NetworkObject+0x28 id, 9, 1). Offline the result is harmless: the send is dropped, the vote only records, and NetworkCheatManager+0x88 stays empty. But it shows the game's cheat code is live in RVNG matches regardless of the online flag.
sources: mx.py q/dis DM vtable slots (this session)

findings.topic: Cheat reports leaving the PC at match end, and persisted abuse records
findings.finding: OnGameFinish 0x1471c9580 (+0xab8 of the online GM) calls NetworkCheatManager 0x1474a3830 (at 0x1471c965e). That function walks NetworkCheatManager+0x88 and, for each record, calls web API 0x1479b3e60(UDM+0x12a0, ..., type+0x2710, functor 0x14cb66d20), gated by 0x147926ce0. Offline +0x88 is never filled. With +0x1fa=1 and +0x30=0 it is, so a cheat report goes to Bandai whenever the LiveWebAPI gate passes. ULiveAccountSaveGame.CheatRecordList (+0x430, SaveGame TArray<FLiveCheatRecordData{EChronicleAbuseType,Count}>) and FChronicleMatchmakerJoinLobbyArgs.AbuseTypes (+0x40) show that abuse types are saved and later sent to the Chronicle matchmaker; EChronicleAbuseType appears to be the cheat type + 1. I did not find who writes +0x430 (searched the anti-cheat and cheat-manager code; no hit).

findings.topic: Model A (offline host, +0x1fa = +0x1f9 = 0 on both PCs): online behaviour that is lost
findings.finding:
Lost or skipped:
- network objects for planes and game objects (the setup chunk 0x147d13e7c never calls +0xc60/+0xc58/+0xc68; role byte +0xed8 stays 1; the StrixManager+0x2e0 id map stays empty)
- the router has no targets
- report-only damage 0x147d1037d: TakeDamage applies locally
- the server-score path: the score function runs locally because !+0x1fa, and ScoreAddition/ScoreUpdate are never needed
- member tables NM+0x210/+0x410/+0x4d0 and count 0x1474b39e0 = 0; the host test is true on both PCs
- wait bookkeeping and the timers NM+0x61c/+0x620/+0x624/+0x630
- the indirect-kill window NM+0x740 and the 0x739 logic
- MRMM aircraft-info web request 0x147491990
- cheat records in NetworkCheatManager+0x88 (so no web cheat report), the vote kick, LatencyCheck pings, 'room members is 0' and the other supervision kicks
- sync-time offset (0x14528cb50 skipped)
- results with server rewards
- UI 'online' states (0x14818a6d0 returns 0)
Still running offline: the combat-zone and damage checks when RVNG drives the network handlers, and OnGameFinish -> 0x1474a3830 (nothing to send).

findings.topic: Model B (local stand-in: +0x1fa = 1, Strix global null): paths RVNG would have to detour
findings.finding:
Crash risk is low throughout: no path found dereferences a missing Strix object, because every global read is null-tested. The cost is behaviour and outside traffic:
1. Never set +0x1f9; it causes an immediate room-lost kick (0x1474ad748 -> 0x1474b5650).
2. Member queries 0x1474efb30/0x1474efc20/0x1474b39e0 return 0. Both PCs get member id 0 and both pass the host test 0x1474b38d0, so network ids (NetworkObject+0x28) collide. Detour all three to answer from RVNG's session.
3. Timers NM+0x610..0x634 (0x1474b94f0) need answers or a disarm, otherwise error 0x1474b9d80.
4. MRMM 0x147491990 sends a UDM+0xfb0 web request when that object exists. Detour it or force gate 0x147959480 false.
5. ReportCheat fills NetworkCheatManager+0x88, which OnGameFinish turns into the web cheat report 0x1474a3830 -> 0x1479b3e60. Make 0x1474b8bb0 a no-op.
6. TakeDamage becomes report-only and DM leaves NM+0x739 clear. RVNG must inject DamageClient through the router 0x1474ef630, and the cheat check 0x1474a3cb0 validates it.
7. The client stops scoring, so RVNG must make ScoreUpdate.
8. Server-made messages (PreparingMissionEnd, RealTime, NpcRandomLotteryResult, EvaluationList, RequestRespawn) have to be synthesised.
9. The phaseIndex room property 0x1474ed840 stays not-found; detour 0x1471c1050.
10. The vote kick 0x1474a3430 is unreachable because 0x1474b3860 is false.
11. Never inject EasyAntiCheatPeerData, Cheat, KickPlayer or LatencyCheck.
12. Results and UI enter online branches (0x1480ecce0 messenger/party/web calls, 0x14813a280.. when +0x30 is 1 or 2). The messenger is null-guarded; the web calls depend on the LiveWebAPI gates.

rvngImplications: Use model A, with explicit calls instead of a global flag. Keep ULiveStrixManager (GI+0x910) +0x1fa = +0x1f9 = +0x1f8 = 0 on both PCs for the whole session, and never call 0x1474ec7e0, 0x1452390d0 or the InitializeStrixNetwork thunks 0x1451eb590/0x1451eb770. Each tick, assert that *(0x14e4c5818) == 0 and that GI+0x930 ULiveNetworkP2P +0x28 == 0. If either is non-zero, stop RVNG mode and leave to the menu.

If RVNG needs network objects (for example to reuse the remote-copy code), call the plane vslots +0xc60/+0xc58/+0xc68 itself, the way setup chunk 0x147d13e7c would. At most, flip +0x1fa to 1 only around that one call on the game thread, then restore 0 before returning. Never leave +0x1fa set across a frame, and never set +0x1f9.

report.summary: All addresses are from the 2026-11-02 AceCombat8.exe (551,201,904 bytes). The game travels to a mission by MissionID: it reads UserDataManager (GI+0x8e0) +0xf38, looks up the FLiveLevelTable row with 0x14734d370(InfoMgr, id), and passes row+0x48 (MapReference) with an empty options FString to ULiveMapChangeManager (GI+0x888)::RequestChangeMap 0x147901bf0. The caller is the transition function 0x147570da0, which then calls the NetworkManager prepare step 0x1474ae080. Online, +0xf38 is written by ULiveNetworkManager::OnJoinRoomComplete (0x1474b8704) from the Strix member property 'missionId'. Offline it is written only by menu code, which Survival already does by hand. The online game mode builds both pilots during the SpawnPlayerPlane state. LoadPlayerPlane Enter (0x1471bd0f0) starts an async load of every member's aircraft class and sets GM+0x5f1=1; LoadPlayerPlane Tick (0x1471c6450) waits for it to return to 0. SpawnPlayerPlane Enter (0x1471c6460) calls the local spawn 0x1471b66a0, which takes everything from UserDataManager and writes role 3 online or 1 offline. It then calls the remote loop 0x1471b7430, which takes everything from two unreflected room tables: NetworkManager+0x410 (members by slot, filled from the matchmaker's ConfirmedResult) and MissionRoomMemberManager+0x40 AircraftSelectorMap (one ULiveAircraftSelector per member, filled by FLiveMessageAircraftSelect). Offline both tables are empty and NM+0x3d8 (the loop count) is 0, so no opponent is spawned. Survival's campaign mode runs the same two calls (0x1478d26a0) with nothing happening, which proves the empty case is harmless. To let the game's own remote spawn 0x1471b84f0 create the opponent, RVNG has to fill NM+0x3d8, NM+0x410 and the selector map with the opponent's userId, name, aircraft id, weapons, parts, skin and emblems from its P2P link, before LoadPlayerPlane Enter. None of these functions contacts a server. The online-only steps are the Chronicle matchmaker, Strix JoinRoom/OnJoinRoomComplete, AircraftSelect relay, the MRMM web-API request 0x147491990 (gated on StrixManager+0x1fa), and the UDM+0xfb0 API calls. Compared with Survival's manual SV_CoopSpawnPP, the native path also sets plane+0x2200/+0x2210 (userId and gamer tag), +0x3c00 (slot+1), +0x53b8 and NetworkObject+0x28 (netId | 2<<56), the cost and level fields (+0xfcc..+0xfdc, +0x3ab8) that the DM score and respawn tables scale by, a preloaded class, and the timing before TimeSync, so DM's faction assigner and rank list include the opponent. One major risk is static: offline the local plane has no NetworkObject, so DM's assigner 0x1471e0230 sorts it first on both PCs. Each pilot is then Alpha on their own PC and both start at Start_Alpha0, so RVNG must fix factions or ids. Other unknowns need in-game tests: whether +0x5f1 clears offline (the clearing lambda is virtualized), side effects of a non-zero NM+0x3d8, and selector NetworkObject creation offline.

findings.topic: Mission ID field and its writers
findings.finding: UserDataManager (GI+0x8e0) +0xf38 is the current MissionID. Other native fields next to it: +0xf3c is the target ELiveLevelID, written e.g. to 0x1869b (OnlineLobby) at 0x147eca011 and to 0x18697 (OnlineStartup) at 0x1474d912f; +0xf4c is npcDifficultyId; +0xf60 is a mode byte. Menu writers in the 2026-11-02 build: 0x147b80dbb (mode 1, mission id clamped to 1..31, campaign), 0x147b00979 and 0x147b01105 (mode 2, free mission), and 0x14783a710, 0x147b5f91c, 0x147b6acf5, 0x147b5cdfd, 0x147b022d2, 0x147a7d230, 0x14756c74d, 0x1476f1dfc, 0x1478dc17f and 0x1471ba0a7 (the last copies UDM+0xe14 to +0xf38 when +0xe12 is set). The only online writer is 0x1474b8704 in ULiveNetworkManager::OnJoinRoomComplete (chunk 0x1474b8478, which leas 'ULiveNetworkManager::OnJoinRoomComplete' 0x14cb676f0). It reads two Strix member properties for the local member (NM+0x520) through 0x1474ed840, 'missionId' (UTF-16 at 0x14beed678) and 'npcDifficultyId' (0x14beed568), writes them to UDM+0xf38 and +0xf4c, and sets NM+0x4c8=1. Survival's runtime writes +0xf38 and +0xf60 directly before going to the hangar, and the sortie then loads that mission row's map.

findings.topic: Travel to a mission by id (MapChangeManager path)
findings.finding: ULiveMapChangeManager is GI+0x888 (FPropertyParams 0x14c6ff5b0, offset 0x888; getter 0x147ece600). Its reflected members are TransitionLoader +0x40, TravelLoader +0x48, CurrentRequestInfo +0x50 and PendingRequestInfo +0xa0. Its request function is 0x147901bf0(MCM, const FSoftObjectPath*, FString* options, ..., delegate), and every caller passes an empty FString for the options. There are two lookups. ChangeLevel 0x147ec9e40(world, ELiveLevelID) uses 0x14734ca30(InfoMgr, levelId), which returns a row whose +0x48 is the soft path; examples are 0x147eca160 (MainMenu, id 2) and 0x147ec9fc0 (OnlineLobby 0x1869b). Mission travel by id is done in the transition handler 0x147570da0, which is called through the weak-delegate thunk 0x147581560. That function reads UDM+0xf38 and +0xf3c. In its default branch (transition state from 0x147568f80 not 9/0xb/0xc, and 0x1475692a0 false) it calls 0x14734d370(InfoMgr, MissionID), which returns &FLiveLevelTable, and then RequestChangeMap(MCM, &row+0x48 MapReference, empty options) at 0x147570f85. After that it calls ULiveNetworkManager 0x1474ae080 at 0x1475710d8. With no '?game=' option, the loaded PL_DM_00x world's own LiveWorldSettings.DefaultGameMode (BP_ChronicleDeathMatchGameMode) is used. The 0xb/0xc branches instead call 0x147956d00(UDM+0xfb0), an API-controller object (not resolved), and ChangeLevel(Startup/MainMenu). Other RequestChangeMap callers: 0x1471af6b0, 0x1471b0d50, 0x1471c5edb (game modes, e.g. Result travel), 0x147110470, 0x147116170, 0x147848da3, 0x147b5dd47, 0x148188b3d.

findings.topic: Online path from match found to mission load
findings.finding: 1. In the Chronicle matchmaker (ULiveMatchmakerClientController OnMatchedFunc/OnConfirmedFunc, a Bandai service), the NM dispatcher 0x1474ae9e7 calls 0x1474b2310(NM, const FChronicleMatchmakerConfirmedResult*). That sets NM+0x3b0 = MatchmakingId, NM+0x3d8 = Players (+0x10), NM+0x3c0 = MissionProgramId (+0x30), and rebuilds NM+0x410 from Members (stride 0xc0) with slot = running index, userId, Username and Team. 0x1474b2610 is a variant that writes NM+0x3d8 from +0x10 and NM+0x3c0 from +0x1c. 2. NM joins the Strix room ('ULiveNetworkManager::JoinRoomByMatchedInfo()' 0x14cb67690, UStrixNetworkFacade::JoinRoom), a Strix service. OnJoinRoomComplete then sets UDM+0xf38/+0xf4c from the 'missionId' and 'npcDifficultyId' properties. 3. MRMM 0x147490bc0, called from 0x14748e610, creates one ULiveAircraftSelector per NM+0x410 member (NewObject through 0x14749cbd0, plus a ULiveNetworkAircraftSelector at sel+0x188). The aircraft-select phase follows: SystemObject sends FLiveMessageAircraftSelectStart (0x1474ce870); each member sends FLiveMessageAircraftSelect (0x14749b0c9) and receives the others' (handler 0x14749b390 -> 0x147490af0). The local selector is filled from UDM by 0x147491460, called from 0x14818a8c0. 4. Travel: 0x147570da0 -> RequestChangeMap(MapReference), then 0x1474ae080. 0x1474ae080 clears NM+0x4d0 through 0x1474b5b10 if StrixManager+0x1fa==0; otherwise, per mode type through a jump table, it builds NM+0x4d0 from NM+0x410 and MRMM (0x1474b5d90). It then calls MRMM 0x147494ba0 for bot preparation. 5. In the DM map, ALiveOnlineGameMode's state machine runs.

The Tick then reads the Strix client 0x14e4c5818 (null-checked), sets LoadingPercentageManager (GI+0x890) through 0x147900f60, calls NM 0x1474b5950(1), and advances. +0xc70 Enter PostNetworkInitialize is 0x1416b1b70 (no-op); +0xc78 Tick PostNetworkInitialize is 0x1471c6430 = jmp NextState. +0xc80 Enter LoadPlayerPlane is 0x1471c6440 = jmp 0x1471bd0f0. +0xc88 Tick LoadPlayerPlane is 0x1471c6450, 'cmp byte [rcx+0x5f1],0; je NextState'. +0xc90 Enter SpawnPlayerPlane is 0x1471c6460: local spawn 0x1471b66a0, remote loop 0x1471b7430, AI-bot world subsystem (0x147ba34b0 = world+0x888 subsystem of class 0x146cfd490) -> 0x147ba3590 start loading, then LoadingPercentage. +0xc98 Tick SpawnPlayerPlane is 0x1471c6520: it returns while subsystem+0x60 != 0; if 0x147ba7180(world,1) and 0x147ba7250 it runs lambda 0x1471bd590; it builds MRMM 0x1474940c0(MRMM, &set, NM mode type 0x1474b6b40), a bot-id set with special cases for mode types 2, 9 and 10, runs lambda 0x1471bdec0, calls 0x1471ccf90, then NextState and clears a GI timer (0x147ece650 +0x68/+0x70). findings.topic: Byte GM+0x5f1 (LoadPlayerPlane gate)
findings.finding: The ALiveGameMode ctor zeroes the word at +0x5f0 at 0x1471b4872. Enter LoadPlayerPlane 0x1471bd0f0 builds a unique TArray<FSoftObjectPath> (stride 0x20) of aircraft classes. The local entry is InfoMgr row 0x14734d490(InfoMgr, UDM+0xd28)+0x38. Only if vf+0xa10 IsOnlineMode is true (DM slot 322 = 0x1416bb960, returns true), it adds for i < NM+0x3d8: memberId = 0x1474b1890(NM,&s,i), aircraftId = (MRMM+0x40)[memberId]->+0x78, and that row's +0x38 path. If the list is non-empty it writes 'mov byte [r14+0x5f1],1' (0x1471bd369), the only plain writer of +0x5f1 in this build. It then asks the loader at GI+0x880 through 0x1478fc1f0(loader, &list, delegate) with callback 0x1471bd4d0, bound to the GM by a weak pointer (index +0xc, serial). 0x1471bd4d0 is 'jmp 0x15bdf7db0' into the protected section, so the clear back to 0 is presumably in that completion callback, but this is not visible statically. The Tick advances when +0x5f1 == 0.

findings.topic: Remote spawn loop 0x1471b7430 and per-member wrapper 0x1471b9330
findings.finding: 0x1471b7430(GM): localNetId = MRMM 0x147492940(MRMM, &localUserId), where localUserId = FString *(UDM+0xfd0)+0x0; it returns sel+0x2c or -1. For i in [0, NM+0x3d8): if 0x147492730(MRMM, i) != localNetId, call 0x1471b9330(GM, i). 0x147492730 walks AircraftSelectorMap for the selector with +0x30 == i and returns its +0x2c, or -1. A slot with no selector therefore equals -1 and is skipped when the local member also has no selector. 0x1471b9330(GM, i) has two paths. Replay path: when GI+0xb08 exists and GM+0x663 is set, the aircraft id comes from (GI+0xb08)+0x8258. Normal path: memberId = 0x1474b1890(NM,&s,i); aircraftId = 0x147492b70(MRMM, &memberId) = sel+0x78, or 0 if absent; row = 0x14734d490(InfoMgr, aircraftId); the class soft path at row+0x38 is resolved with 0x141aa6e80 or else synchronously loaded with 0x141aa6c90. The class must be a UClass, and then 0x1471b84f0(GM, i, class) is called. With no member data offline (NM+0x3d8 = 0) nothing happens.

findings.topic: Factions and initial placement in DM
findings.finding: In this build the DM faction assigner 0x1471e0230 (SoloPVP slot +0xa30) runs at the end of TimeSync. It sorts CachedPlayerPlanes by the uint32 at NetworkObject+0x28, using 0 when there is no network object (prior research), and gives Alpha+i and the name 'ALPHA'..'ZULU'. The NM+0x4d0 entry keyed by plane+0x2200 overrides this only if present, and offline 0x1474ae080 clears NM+0x4d0. The remote copy's key is its netId (low dword of netId | 2<<56), while the offline local plane has no NetworkObject (key 0). So on each PC the local plane sorts first and becomes Alpha: host sees host=Alpha and guest=Bravo, guest sees guest=Alpha and host=Bravo. TeleportPlayers (0x1471c6c90, picker 0x147391240) places each PC's own plane at Start_Alpha0, so both pilots would start at the same spot (0,-7500) in their own sims. 0x1471b75f0, called from the online GM at 0x1471c5742, is a per-player-plane post-setup. It runs lambda 0x1471b7840, which looks up NM+0x4d0 (slot rule: Alpha idx<=8, Bravo idx+4, others 0) and spawns a companion through 0x147ba3be0 only when MRMM+0x40's flag byte allows it. It also registers the plane's netId into world-manager objects' +0xd98/+0xd88 lists (0x147d27b90).
sources: pvp_research/targeting-verify/fn_1471e0230.txt and digest verifier note (sort key NetworkObject+0x28)

findings.topic: Native remote spawn vs Survival's manual SV_CoopSpawnPP
findings.finding: Survival (verified in game) copies the remote spawn's steps by hand: deferred SpawnActor, ALiveNetworkDummyController Possess, vslot +0xc60, +0xed8 = 2, loadout through the loadout setter, +0xfa0/+0xfa1, skin +0xfa4, emblems +0xfb8, flags +0xfc8, callsign +0x6e8, ObjName +0x6d8, FinishSpawning. The native path adds the following. +0x2200 userId and +0x2210 gamer tag: the tag line shows only in an online GM (0x147edaf50), which DM is. +0x3c00 = slot+1. +0x53b8 and NetworkObject+0x28 = netId|2<<56, the DM sort key and the router's type-2 key. +0x3ab8 level, +0xfcc/+0xfd0/+0xfd4/+0xfd8. +0xfac/+0xfb0/+0xfb4, probably weathering (COOP2MP). +0xfdc, the cost value from 0x147933ff0 that the online cost tables can scale score and respawn by (inferred). The class is preloaded in LoadPlayerPlane, so there is no sync-load hitch. The timing is inside SpawnPlayerPlane, before TimeSync, so the copy is in CachedPlayerPlanes for the faction assigner, TeleportPlayers and CallStartMatch's ScoreRankList. 0x1471b75f0 post-setup also runs.

rvngImplications: Mission travel: write UserDataManager (GI+0x8e0) +0xf38 = 160010 (or 160020/30/40/60), as Survival writes 9101 (survival_rt.c:617-618), then travel. Either use the game's sortie/transition (0x147570da0 default branch -> 0x14734d370 -> RequestChangeMap 0x147901bf0(GI+0x888, &row+0x48, empty FString)), or call 0x147901bf0 directly with the DM row's MapReference and no ?game= option. Do not call 0x147ec9fc0 (OnlineLobby) or any branch of 0x147570da0 that calls 0x147956d00(UDM+0xfb0). Find 0x147901bf0, 0x14734d370 and 0x147570da0 by signature; the VAs are from the 2026-11-02 build.

Keep ULiveStrixManager (GI+0x910)+0x1fa == 0 for the whole session. That keeps 0x147491990's web request, the role-3 branch, MRMM loadout overrides of the local plane and all Strix queries unreached. The cost is that the local plane gets role 1 and no NetworkObject, so RVNG writes role 3 itself after spawn (the 0x1471b697c equivalent).

Before LoadPlayerPlane Enter runs (that is, before or right after the map's GM is constructed, while still in states 1-2), fill the room tables with the game's own functions. Call NM 0x1474b2310(NM, &ConfirmedResult), with a locally built FChronicleMatchmakerConfirmedResult {MatchmakingId any, Players=2, Members[0]={userId host, Username host gamer tag, Team 0}, Members[1]={guest...}, MissionProgramId 0}. That sets NM+0x3d8 = 2 and NM+0x410 slots 0 and 1. Then call MRMM 0x147490bc0(MRMM) to create the two ULiveAircraftSelectors, and 0x147491460(MRMM, &localUserId, 1) to fill the local one from UDM. Check first that 0x1474b3770 is skipped (NM+0x4b8 <= 0) or harmless.

Write the opponent's selector fields from the RVNG P2P 'hi' packet: +0x2c netId (non-zero, distinct: host 1, guest 2 on both PCs), +0x30 slot, +0x78 aircraftId, +0x7c level, +0x80, +0x88 TArray<int32> weapons, +0x98 TArray<int32> parts, +0xa8 skin, +0xc0 {special1, special2}, +0xd0/+0xd4/+0xd8, +0xdc flag mask, +0xe0 TArray<int32> emblems, +0x100/+0x104/+0x108. Use the game's TArray allocation (the copy-assign used at 0x1416d9f10 / 0x1416dd490) and never raw pointers. Each PC sends exactly the values 0x147491460 would put in its own local selector.

Make the local plane's userId match: plane+0x2200 comes from *(UDM+0xfd0)+0x0. Use that same FString as the local member's Members[i].userId so that 0x147492940 (localNetId) finds the local selector, and the remote loop skips the local slot and spawns only the opponent through 0x1471b84f0.

Fix DM factions consistently. Hook the return of 0x1471e0230 (SoloPVP vtable slot +0xa30), or the TeleportPlayers Enter at +0xcd0 = 0x1471c6c30, and SetFaction(host plane, Alpha) / SetFaction(guest plane, Bravo) through 0x147d0b980 on both PCs before TeleportPlayers places them. Without this both pilots are Alpha on their own PC and both start at Start_Alpha0. The alternative is to give the local plane a NetworkObject (vslot +0xc60) with +0x28 = netId so the sort agrees on both PCs.

Hook (log only) 0x1471b84f0's entry and 0x1471b87da to confirm the opponent spawns with role 2. Then let RVNG's flight layer drive that ALiveNetworkDummyController-possessed plane exactly as Survival drives its manual copy. Do not destroy or re-spawn it mid-level (Survival hard rule).

If GM+0x5f1 never returns to 0 offline (Tick 0x1471c6450 stalls), patch nothing in the virtualized lambda. Instead clear GM+0x5f1 once the plane classes in the list are loaded, or detour Tick 0x1471c6450 to advance after a timeout.

Fallback that needs no room tables: let the native local spawn run, and spawn the opponent with Survival's SV_CoopSpawnPP during SpawnPlayerPlane (before TimeSync). Additionally write +0x2200, +0x2210, +0x3c00 = 2, +0x53b8 and NetworkObject+0x28 = netId|2<<56, and +0x3ab8/+0xfcc..+0xfdc, copying the opponent's own spawn values from the P2P packet.
blockers: The async-load completion lambda 0x1471bd4d0 jumps into the protected section (0x15bdf7db0), so it is not statically shown that it clears GM+0x5f1. LoadPlayerPlane could stall offline.
NM+0x3d8 != 0 offline has unexamined readers (0x147490ac9, 0x1474ae821, 0x1474b9548, 0x1474f8d0a) that could enter online-only code.
Writes of selector weapons +0x88 and parts +0x98 (the AircraftSelect payload parse 0x147490af0) and the formula that assigns the selector netId +0x2c were not traced. RVNG must write them directly.

Whether creating ULiveNetworkAircraftSelector objects (sel+0x188) and the remote plane's vslot +0xc60 NetworkObject offline tries to register with or send to Strix is unknown. Prior research says sends return quietly without the Strix client 0x14e4c5818, but registration (+0x2b8) was not traced for this path.
0x1474b2310 calls 0x1474b3770 when NM+0x4b8 > 0; not examined.
The UDM+0xfb0 object's class is not resolved; it is treated as a web-API controller (inferred) and must stay unreached.
The DM rows' FLiveLevelTable.LevelId and how the offline hangar sortie reaches 0x147570da0 for a DM row were not checked. Survival proves the hangar route only for a campaign-type row.
openQuestions: At the main menu (UE4SS, offline), dump UDM (GI+0x8e0): +0xf38, +0xf3c, +0xf4c, +0xf60, +0xd28, +0xd2c/+0xd2d, +0xd30, the +0xd38 TArray, the +0xdd8 TArray, the +0xde8 TArray, and *(+0xfd0) {+0x0 FString, +0x10 FString, +0x78, +0x7c}. Are the local userId and name non-empty offline?

Set UDM+0xf38 = 160010 and travel (hangar sortie, or a direct 0x147901bf0 with the row's MapReference). Log the GM class (expect BP_ChronicleDeathMatchGameMode_C), the state byte +0x758 every frame and GM+0x5f1. Hook 0x147901bf0 during an ordinary campaign sortie and log its FSoftObjectPath and options FString arguments to confirm the empty options string and which caller (0x147570f85?) issues mission travel.

Before travel, call 0x1474b2310 with a two-member ConfirmedResult and 0x147490bc0 + 0x147491460, then fill the opponent's selector by hand. Log NM+0x3d8, the NM+0x410 count, the MRMM+0x40 count, and 0x147492940 / 0x147492730 results for slots 0 and 1. Does 0x1471b84f0 run exactly once with the opponent's slot and class, and does the copy show its skin, emblems, specials, gamer tag (+0x2210) and ObjName?

Log every read of NM+0x3d8 (hardware or code breakpoints at 0x147490ac9, 0x1474ae821, 0x1474b9548, 0x1474f8d0a) during that test. Does any of them run with +0x1fa == 0, and does anything try to reach Strix (hook 0x1474a2190 and 0x1474ed840 and log callers)?

Log both planes' +0x3b2, NetworkObject (+0xed0) and +0x28 right after 0x1471e0230 on both PCs, and the positions after TeleportPlayers (state 8). Confirm the 'both local = Alpha' prediction and that a SetFaction fix before TeleportPlayers places the host at Start_Alpha0 and the guest at Start_Bravo0 on both PCs.
Compare the native copy's +0xfdc (cost) with the local plane's +0xfdc for the same airset. Check whether DM score per kill and respawn time scale with it (DT_PlayerAircraftCost).

Two more UDM+0xf38 writers were missed. 0x147848cec (in 0x147848ab5) is replay playback: f38 = replay record +0x8268, then 0x14734d370 and RequestChangeMap at 0x147848da3, with no 0x1474ae080. 0x147ab8221 writes f38=1 and f60=1. Static.

Concrete in-game tests. (1) Log 0x147568f80's return and UDM+0xf3c at 0x147570da0 entry during a stock sortie and during RVNG's DM travel. Expect type 9 with f3c outside 19..49 for MissionID travel. (2) After travel, while GM+0x758 is 1 or 2, write NM+0x4d0 (host 1, guest 2) on both PCs. Then log every plane's +0x3b2 and callsign (+0x6e8) after 0x1471e0230 returns. (3) Hook 0x1475706e0's return with NM+0x3d8 set before travel versus after, to see whether the sortie stalls. (4) After the match, restore NM+0x3d8=0, clear the tables, run a campaign sortie and confirm 0x1471b84f0 is not called.

report.summary: I walked all 20 ELiveOnlineGameModeState states of ALiveDeathMatchGameMode (vtable 0x14c693718; online base 0x14c980e98) on the 2026-11-02 AceCombat8.exe. The deathmatch class overrides only the GamePlaying tick (+0xd40 = 0x1471df440), OnGameFinish (+0xab8 = 0x1471df1f0) and the start hook (+0xb28). Every other Enter and Tick belongs to ALiveOnlineGameMode. The online Tick 0x1471c54e0 adds dt to +0x57c and calls the per-state Tick. SetState 0x1471c6020 and NextState 0x1471c6150 call the Enter functions. NextState also writes the local state into the NetworkManager member-state TMap at NM+0x210, keyed by the Strix member id online or by 0 offline. Every "wait for members" point compares CountAtLeast(NM+0x210, N) (the protected thunk 0x1474cc700) with MemberCount 0x1474b39e0. MemberCount is the live Strix room member list and returns 0 offline, so offline every such check passes on the first tick. A correction to earlier work: NM+0x538 is not a member count but the last FLiveMessageError code. Offline the machine has exactly two blocking gates. The first is SyncStartMatch's 0x1471c1050, which needs the Strix room property "phaseIndex" to be at least 1. No client code writes it, and online a 35 s timer raises "client error : mission start timeout". The second is GameTerminating, which needs the PreparingMissionEnd stage GM+0x80c to be at least 2. Online that value is written only at the end of a server-driven chain: the server-made FLiveMessageMissionRewardUser triggers a LiveWebAPI request (UserData+0x1220), then a user-data step, then a save, then the delegate 0x1471d47c4. Offline the stage stays at 1 for ever. Leaving GamePlaying works offline: OnGameFinish starts a 3.0 s ULiveOnlineMissionEndSequence whose finish (0x14747d2a0 → 0x1471bc980 → vf+0xb48 = NextState) moves the machine into GameTerminating. The clock is local: FinishTime = BeginPlay time + GM+0x498 seconds (in 100 ns ticks), set by 0x1471b5160 on the post-BeginPlay delegate 0x14dd876b8. The clock stays paused until CallStartMatch, and offline time-up runs locally because the host test is true. GM+0x498 defaults to 480 s and is probably overwritten from the level's MissionConfig through the protected vf+0xaa8. SyncEvaluation and the Result map's ResultState sync both pass offline. Results hold only local evaluation data, because rewards arrive only from the server and LiveWebAPI. For RVNG, staying offline (+0x1fa = 0) needs only three things. Set the mission id before load. Answer the phaseIndex gate by detouring 0x1471c1050, which also works as RVNG's synchronized start barrier. Write GM+0x80c = 2 when state 15 is entered. Setting +0x1fa = 1 instead would arm several online-only timeouts and presence checks that RVNG would then have to defeat one by one.

findings.topic: Build, method, scratch output
findings.finding: All VAs are from AceCombat8.exe of 2026-11-02 (551,201,904 bytes, base 0x140000000). I reused the prior dumps: flow/online_gm2.txt (0x1471ad000-0x1471e3000), modes/dis_region.txt, seam/dis_net_region.txt (0x147480000-0x14751ffff) and flow/states.txt. New queries were memory-light mmap batch scripts using seam-verify/mx.py plus llvm-objdump, never Exe(), one process at a time: deep-sync/tools/q1.py to q13.py, with extractors fx.py and fc.py. The extracts are in deep-sync/*.txt (states_a, nm_a, nm_b, sys_h1, sys_h2, phase, pme, pme_net, stage2, tick, end, clock_a/b/c, result_a, q1-q13). Full path of deep-sync: <scratchpad>/pvp_research/deep-sync/. No game log on this build contains any online-state string; I searched build/autotest/runs/**/survival_logs/*.log. Everything below is therefore static or inferred.

findings.topic: Dispatcher, SetState, NextState
findings.finding: The online Tick (actor tick slot +0x4f8) is 0x1471c54e0. It calls Super 0x144442d50. If GM+0x520 (match started, read by vf+0xb70) is set and GM+0x521 (finished, read by vf+0xb80) is not, it checks IsTimeUp 0x1471b9950 and on true calls vf+0xb30. Online only, it looks up each plane's name (plane+0x2200) in MissionRoomMemberManager+0x40 (AircraftSelectorMap). If the selector is missing or its +0x28 is 0, it calls 0x14193fa80(NM+0x6a8), then 0x1471b75f0(GM, plane) (disconnect handling) and sets plane+0x53c8=1. It then adds dt to +0x57c and dispatches the state Tick. Tick slots by state: 1:+0xc68, 2:+0xc78, 3:+0xc88, 4:+0xc98, 5:+0xca8, 6:+0xcb8, 7:+0xcc8, 8:+0xcd8, 9:+0xce8, 10:+0xcf8, 11:+0xd10, 12:+0xd20, 13:+0xd30, 14: 0x1471bca40 then +0xd40, 15:+0xd50, 16:+0xd60, 17:+0xd70, 18:+0xd88, 19:+0xd98, 20:+0xda8. SetState 0x1471c6020 stores the state at +0x758, zeroes +0x57c and jumps to the Enter slot (2:+0xc70 ... 12:+0xd18, 13:+0xd28, 14:+0xd38, 15:+0xd48, 16:+0xd58, 17:+0xd68, 18:+0xd80, 19:+0xd90, 20:+0xda0). NextState 0x1471c6150 does nothing at state 0x14. Otherwise it increments the state and calls 0x1474cc910(NM+0x210, memberId, state), with memberId = 0x1474efb30(strix, NM+0x520) when +0x1fa is set, else 0. When +0x1fa is set and NM+0x4c0 exists, it writes the NetworkObject+0x88 message buffer (+0x20 id, +0x24 state, +0x19 = 1 dirty). It then calls SetState. TeleportPlayers' tick has an inline copy of this at 0x1471c6e6c. A scan of the whole exe found only these direct writers of +0x758: ctor 0x1471c516d (=1), 0x1471c6022, 0x1471c617a, 0x1471c6e59 (=0x14 Replay), 0x1471c6e81 and 0x1471c6f19.

findings.topic: Member-state table NM+0x210, CountAtLeast 0x1474cc700, MemberCount 0x1474b39e0, NM+0x520/+0x538
findings.finding: NM+0x210 is a TMap<int32 memberId, uint64 state>. Its TSet layout is: Data +0, Num +8, NumFree +0x34, Hash +0x38/+0x40, HashSize +0x48, element size 0x18 (key +0, value +8, next +0x10). Setter 0x1474cc910(map, key, value) returns true when the value changed. Writers: NextState (0x1471c61c8, 0x1471c6ed0), 0x1471b9888, and the GameModeState receive handler 0x1474cf099. Sibling tables use the same setter: NM+0x260 PhaseState, NM+0x2b0 ResultState, NM+0x300 IGCState ((id<<8)|2, local writer 0x1474ae770). CountAtLeast 0x1474cc700 is 'jmp 0x15c19a270' into protected code. Its callers use it as 'number of members whose value >= N'. TimeSync uses N=5 and, for the client, N=6 > 0. The other callers are WaitingSpawnedAIs 7, WaitingIGCOpeningStart 9, WaitingIGCOpeningEnd 0xb, WaitingIGCEndingStart 0x10, SyncEvaluation 0x12, the IGC tick on NM+0x300, the Result GM on NM+0x2b0 >= 2, and 0x147490a80 (NM+0x350 vs NM+0x3d8). MemberCount 0x1474b39e0 returns 0 when StrixManager+0x1fa == 0. Otherwise it returns the size of 0x145294cc0(strix client 0x14e4c5818, &list, NM+0x520), which is also 0 when the client is null. NM+0x520 is the Strix channel id, not a member index. It is the key into the strix+0x60 channel map, and WaitingNetworkInitialize opens channel W"default" (0x14b777ab8). NM+0x538 is not a member count. Handler 0x1474b9080 (FLiveMessageError, getter 0x1452afdc0, called from the router at 0x1474efb07, log text 'FLiveMessageError : ') stores the error code msg+0x8 there, and the NM tick reads it. Consequence offline: every 'count >= MemberCount' barrier compares against 0 and passes on its first tick, whatever 0x1474cc700 does internally, because a count is never negative.

findings.topic: FLiveMessageGameModeState: sender and consumer
findings.finding: The sender is the SystemObject state slot 0x1474cdb90, registered in the SystemObject slot-87 builder 0x1474ccc30 through 0x1474a1f10. It copies the NM.NetworkObject+0x88 template into a new message (vtable 0x14bfd7570, size 0x40): +0x20 member id, +0x24 state byte, +0x28 int from 0x145239ab0(strix, channel) (0 without a client). It stamps msg+0x8 with the synced clock, sends through 0x1474a2190, and also writes NM+0x658[member] = msg+0x28 through 0x1474ba1f0. The consumer is the SystemObject handler 0x1474cefb0 (getter 0x1452b63b0). It sets NM+0x210[msg+0x20] = msg+0x24 and NM+0x658[msg+0x20] = msg+0x28. While GM vf+0xb70 (match started) is true, it computes the delay (now - msg+0x8) x 1e-7 s and keeps a per-member late counter in NM+0x6a8, incremented when the delay exceeds NM+0x6f8 and reset otherwise. Nothing else consumes it. The sync checks read only NM+0x210.

findings.topic: State 1 WaitingNetworkInitialize
findings.finding: There is no Enter; the ctor 0x1471c5070 sets state 1. Tick +0xc68 = 0x1471c6230. It calls MissionRoomMemberManager (GI+0x958) 0x147491990 and builds W"default". It initializes the synced clock: clk = 0x147907550() (lazy singleton 0x14e5101b8); clk+0x8 = clk+0x10 = 0x147907660() (now); clk+0x18 = 0x14528cb50(strix, &o, NM+0x520) server time, or 0 when the client is null; clk+0x20 = 0. It calls LoadingPercentage (GI+0x890) 0x147900f60(0.5) and NM 0x1474b5950(NM, 1), then NextState unconditionally. Offline: it passes, and synced now = local time since this tick. RVNG needs nothing here.

findings.topic: States 2-4 PostNetworkInitialize, LoadPlayerPlane, SpawnPlayerPlane
findings.finding: State 2: Enter +0xc70 = nullsub 0x1416b1b70; Tick +0xc78 = 0x1471c6430, which is a jmp to NextState. State 3: Enter +0xc80 = 0x1471c6440, which jumps to 0x1471bd0f0. That function starts async loading of the plane assets, sets GM+0x5f1 = 1 and installs completion lambda 0x1471bd4d0. Tick +0xc88 = 0x1471c6450 advances when GM+0x5f1 == 0. State 4: Enter +0xc90 = 0x1471c6460 calls 0x1471b66a0 and 0x1471b7430, the bot manager 0x147ba34b0 → 0x147ba3590, and sets loading to 0.2. Tick +0xc98 = 0x1471c6520 waits while botmgr+0x60 is set. It spawns the local plane (0x147ba7180/0x147ba7250 → 0x1471bd590), builds the member list with 0x1474940c0(MRMM, &list, 0x1474b6b40(NM)), spawns member planes through 0x1471bdec0, then calls 0x1471ccf90 and NextState. No state waits on the network. Offline the member list is empty (inferred), so only the local plane is spawned here. Spawning the opponent belongs to another area.

findings.topic: State 5 TimeSync
findings.finding: Enter +0xca0 = 0x1471c6720 sets LoadingPct+0x50 = 0.5. Online only, it also does sync bookkeeping: NM+0x718 |= 0x40 and NM+0x710 = now. These two fields are written at every sync state; the NM tick never reads them for a timeout. Tick +0xca8 = 0x1471c6810 waits until CountAtLeast(NM+0x210, 5) >= MemberCount. The host (0x1474b38d0) then calls SendGameTime 0x1474b6a60(NM, +0x4a8, +0x4b0, +0x4b8, host), which sends only if +0x1fa is set and NM+0x4c0 exists (0x1474ce270). A non-host instead waits for CountAtLeast(…, 6) > 0. Both then clear the bookkeeping, call vf+0xa30 (the DM faction assigner 0x1471e0230) and 0x1474ae360(NM), and call NextState. Offline: MemberCount is 0 and IsHost is true, so the state passes on the first tick and nothing is sent. RVNG: nothing is needed. This is the natural point to exchange clocks if wanted.

findings.topic: States 6-8 SpawnAIs, WaitingSpawnedAIs, TeleportPlayers
findings.finding: State 6: Enter +0xcb0 = 0x1471c6930 sets loading 0.85 (plus bookkeeping 0x80). Tick +0xcb8 = 0x1471c6a20 waits only when online and 0x147ecd400(world)+0x31 == 0. It then calls vf+0xdc0 (nullsub in Online), spawns bots through world-manager+0x1e8 (0x147847ed0, 0x14786c810, 0x147e00a00, 0x147e00d80) and calls NextState. State 7: Enter +0xcc0 = 0x1471c6b40 sets 0.9. Tick +0xcc8 = 0x1471af9c0 requires CountAtLeast(7) >= MemberCount. State 8: Enter +0xcd0 = 0x1471c6c30 sets 0.95. Tick +0xcd8 = 0x1471c6c90 teleports every plane in world-mgr+0x138, and every bot, to a respawn point (0x147391240 → 0x147d18e20(plane, pt, 1) → 0x147d187f0). If replay flag +0x663 is set it calls vf+0x938 and 0x1471b9c90(1,0) and jumps to state 20; otherwise it advances with the inline NextState. Offline all three pass on their first tick.

findings.topic: States 9-11 WaitingIGCOpeningStart, IGCOpening, WaitingIGCOpeningEnd
findings.finding: State 9: Enter +0xce0 = 0x1471c70c0 sets loading 1.0 and prepares the IGC manager (0x14710a230(world) → 0x147308ff0). Tick +0xce8 = 0x1471c71d0 waits until IGC manager +0xe1 == 0 (loaded) and CountAtLeast(9) >= MemberCount. State 10: Enter +0xcf0 = 0x1471c7270 reads the mission row (InformationManager 0x14734d370 with UserData+0xf38) and its IGC asset, and calls 0x1471cb290(GM, +0x584-1). If 0x147300960 reports an IGC, it binds the finish delegate (vtable 0x14cb37380) and plays it; otherwise it calls vf+0xd00 at once. Tick +0xcf8 = 0x1471afa80 jumps to vf+0xbd0 = Online IGC tick 0x1471ca410. That tick handles skips: skip flag 0x147a59150()+0x60f; local IGCState NM+0x300 = (GM+0x614<<8)|2 through 0x1474ae770; CountAtLeast(NM+0x300, …) >= max(MemberCount, 1); then stop with 0x147307df0 and set GM+0x610 to 3 or 4. The exit vf+0xd00 = 0x1471afef0 fades (0x147ecd710) and calls NextState. State 11: Enter +0xd08 = 0x1471c76c0; Tick +0xd10 = 0x1471c7760 requires CountAtLeast(0xb) >= MemberCount. Offline: state 9 waits only for the IGC load. The IGC plays or is skipped locally, and the skip barrier needs only the local entry because of max(MemberCount, 1). State 11 passes at once. Optionally RVNG can mirror skips.

findings.topic: State 12 SyncStartMatch: the phaseIndex gate (blocking offline)
findings.finding: Enter +0xd18 = 0x1471c7820. Online it does the bookkeeping (0x800) and sets NM+0x620 = INI NPC_RANDOM_LOTTERY_TIMEOUT_SEC (0x14cb677a0, default 30, read with InformationManager 0x14735fbf0) + 5.0. In all cases, if GM.NetworkObject (+0x738) exists, it calls 0x1474a61f0(netobj, 0, 0, 0). Tick +0xd20 = 0x1471c79e0: if 0x1471c1050() is true, it clears the bookkeeping, calls 0x1471be300(GM) and NextState. Otherwise, once (+0x580 == 0 && +0x1fa == 0 && NM+0x538 (error code) > 0), it registers the NM timer 0x1474b8e70(NM, 0x2f4d62, W"SyncStartMatchTick", delegate vtable 0x14cb37588), whose Execute 0x1471d4c70/0x1471d4ce0 calls AbortPath 0x1471c5f70. The gate 0x1471c1050 returns true when the mode type (0x147ec9d20) is 10. Otherwise it calls 0x1474ed840(StrixMgr, NM+0x520, FString W"phaseIndex" (0x14cb3d520), &found, &value) and returns value >= 1. 0x1474ed840 returns found = 0 and value = 0 when strix client 0x14e4c5818 is null. With a client, it reads the property map at +0x68 of the struct produced by 0x1452945a0(strix, &out, channel), through 0x1453a0870. That struct has the shape of a ROOM: id, capacity, a bool defaulting to 1, strings and properties at +0x68. The local-member struct from 0x1452947b0 is only {id, properties at +0x18}. So phaseIndex is a room property, which corrects the earlier 'member property' reading that took NM+0x520 for a member index. The only code reference to the string is this reader (q1 xref scan, SSE and lea forms). No client writes it, so it is set on the server or room side. Online, the NM tick 0x1474b9a43 also calls the gate. While it stays false it counts NM+0x620 down, and at 0 it calls 0x1474b9d80(NM, 0x2f514b, 'client error : mission start timeout'). Required value: at least 1. Offline: the state STALLS for ever (blocking gate 1).

findings.topic: State 13 CallStartMatch
findings.finding: Enter +0xd28 = 0x1471c7c40 calls 0x1471cbb20(GM, 0). That only stores 0 in GI.LiveWebAPI_(+0x970)+0x1f8 and makes no request. It then calls vf+0xc10 = 0x1471c0100, which fills ScoreRankList. Tick +0xd30 = 0x1471afa90 calls the trace marker 0x1471c1240, vf+0x938 (AGameMode::StartMatch 0x1444425d0), NextState, then 0x1471c1300 and 0x1471b9c90(GM, 1, 0). That last call clears pause reason 1 at +0x4c8. When no reasons remain, vf+0xaa0 (0x1471b9df0) shifts Begin, Phase and Finish (+0x4a8/+0x4b0/+0x4b8) by the time spent paused and clears +0x4c0. A host that is online also sends PauseTime through 0x1474b6ad0. Offline it passes in one tick and the match clock starts here.

findings.topic: State 14 GamePlaying and how it is left
findings.finding: Enter +0xd38 = 0x1471c7c70 broadcasts static delegate 0x14dd87670(world) and calls vf+0xb28. For DM that is 0x1471df0d0 → base 0x1471ba2a0, which sets GM+0x520 = 1 at 0x1471ba3ce. It also calls HUD vf+0x818(0) and 0x147893c50(GI+0x908, GM, 1), and fades in. The pre-tick 0x1471bca40 does nothing while PauseManager+0x30 (0x147ec9f60) is set. Otherwise it copies the remaining time to HUD+0x550 when +0x522 is set, fires the time EP triggers through vf+0xb98, and ticks MissionEndSequence (+0x3d8) through vf+0x2d0. The DM Tick 0x1471df440 runs the online tick 0x1471c7e80 (defeat stages, and at <= 60 s left the HUD timer 0x147242970 with +0x522 = +0x750 = 1) and then the VictoryScore check 0x1471df5f0. Leaving: any OnGameFinish (vf+0xab8; reasons 2 Timeup, 3 VictoryScore, 4 Forced, 1 Special) calls +0xac8 0x1471c9800. That creates ULiveOnlineMissionEndSequence (StaticClass 0x146ee7ef0, ctor 0x146eee670, vtable 0x14c85bce0) and calls Start (vf+0x2b8, 3.0 s). Its tick (0x14747d260) accumulates dt. When the 3.0 s are up it calls OnFinished 0x14747d2a0, which calls 0x1471bc980(GM): GM+0x3e0 = 1, then vf+0xb48 (Online slot = 0x1471c6430 = NextState), then the sequence is released. This is the only route from 14 to 15; no other direct NextState caller handles state 14. Offline it works natively. Note that the end sequence does not tick while the game is paused.

findings.topic: Clock: GameTime, RealTime, PauseTime, TimeUp; MissionLimitTime → FinishTime
findings.finding: Synced now = 0x147907660() + clk[0x18] - clk[0x8] + clk[0x20], in 100 ns ticks (factors 1e7 at 0x14d295a8c and 1e-7 at 0x14d292d6c). FinishTime is set offline. 0x1473996a0 (guard flag +0x4f8) broadcasts the static delegates 0x14dd87688, 0x14dd876a0 and 0x14dd876b8(world) at begin-play. 0x1471b5160 is bound to 0x14dd876b8 at 0x1471b4d1a. For its own world it sets clk[0x20] = 0, host = 0x1474b38d0, and Finish = now + round(GM+0x498 x 1e7 + 0.5). It then calls vf+0xa58(now, host) (protected 0x1471b9900) and 0x1471b8290(GM, Begin=now, Phase=now, Finish, bSetByHost=host), which calls the setters vf+0xa68/+0xa70/+0xa78 (0x1471b9920/30/40 writing +0x4a8/+0x4b0/+0x4b8). It then pauses with 0x1471b9c90(GM,1,1), and CallStartMatch unpauses. GM+0x498 is a non-reflected float. The ctor sets it to 480.0 at 0x1471b4a10, and an exe-wide scan found no other GM writer. Slot +0x390 0x1471b5920 (called through Online 0x1471af690) passes WorldSettings.MissionSettings.MissionConfig (world+0x30 → +0x2a0 → +0x500, CDO fallback through vf+0xb40) to vf+0xaa8. vf+0xaa8 is protected (0x1471b9e80 → 0x15bde9600), and the protected code calls SendGameTime at 0x15bde9727. It probably copies MissionLimitTime (config+0x30) into +0x498 (inferred). Remaining time is +0xa88 = 0x1471b9a60: (Finish - (pausedAt or now)) x 1e-7, and 0 when Finish < now. IsTimeUp 0x1471b9950: a host returns GM+0x498 > 0 && remaining <= 0; a client returns true when TMap GM+0x4d0 contains key GM+0x584. Time-up then runs vf+0xb30 0x1471c92f0: if the client is the host and online, it sends TimeUp through NM.NetworkObject 0x1474ce590(+0x584, time). In every case it runs vf+0xb38 0x1471c93c0 (base 0x1471bc880, +0x538 = 2, vf+0xab8). Message consumers on the SystemObject: GameTime 0x1474cff60 calls vf+0xa58(msg+0x20, 1) and 0x1471b8290(msg+0x20 Begin, +0x28 Phase, +0x30 Finish, 1). RealTime 0x1474d00c0 (server-made) sets clk[0x20] = msg+0x20 - local synced time. PauseTime 0x1474d0220 calls vf+0xaa0. TimeUp 0x1474d0370 inserts GM+0x4d0[msg+0x20] = msg+0x28 and calls vf+0xb30. LatencyCheck 0x1474d0ad0 and LatencyResponse 0x1474d0bf0 (server-made) are only registered there, and I did not trace them. Offline every PC is a host, so the clock and time-up are fully local.

findings.topic: State 15 GameTerminating: the PreparingMissionEnd stage (blocking offline)
findings.finding: The online ctor sets +0x804 and +0x80c to 0 (0x1471c5111/0x1471c511d). OnGameFinish (Online 0x1471c9580) runs +0xac8, the NM notify 0x1474b5a30, and the first-time work. Unless the mode type is 10 or 11, it calls 0x1471cb5e0(GM, +0x729, +0x72a). That function returns at once when +0x80c >= 1. Otherwise it sends PreparingMissionEnd through the local plane's network object (+0xed0, 0x1474c69c0), sets +0x80c = 1, and online sets NM+0x624 = PREPARING_MISSION_END_TIMEOUT_SEC + 35. Enter +0xd48 = 0x1471c80f0 is bookkeeping only. Tick +0xd50 = 0x1471c8190: mode type 10 or 11 skips straight to the radio wait. If +0x80c == 0 and 0x1474b3860(NM) (Strix channel connected) is true, it calls 0x1471cb5e0. It goes on only when +0x80c >= 2 or +0x804 == 1. It stops for good when +0x80c == 3. Then it waits until +0x57c >= WaitingRadioInterval (+0x3cc, reflected), or the CDO value 0x1471d17f0()+0xd8 when +0x804 != 0, and calls NextState. Stage 2 is written only by the delegate vtable 0x14cb37658 (Execute 0x1471d47c0, ExecuteIfSafe 0x1471d4750), and that delegate is built only in 0x1471cbeb0. The online chain is: server-made FLiveMessageMissionRewardUser → the ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane handler 0x1474c8f80 copies rewards into UserData(GI+0x8e0)+0xc20. If +0x80c < 2 and the FString NM+0x3b0 is non-empty, it calls the WebAPI request 0x1479bdc40(UserData+0x1220, NM+0x3b0, delegate vtable 0x14cb375f0). That request object binds GI.LiveWebAPI_ through 0x1479297c0. The handler always calls 0x1471cbb20(GM, 1). The request's response goes to 0x1471cbbb0(success, payload), which copies reward info into UserData+0xba8..+0xc18. If 0x147926ce0(UserData+0x10f0) is true, it calls 0x1479b5da0(UserData+0x10f0, UserData+0xc40, delegate vtable 0x14cb376c0 → 0x1471cbeb0), and then tail-calls 0x1471ce3e0. 0x1471cbeb0 runs 0x14793ead0 (the UserData+0x1348 saver, comparing UserData fields) with delegate 0x14cb37658, which writes +0x80c = 2. The online NM tick 0x1474b9b8e..0x1474b9c4b counts NM+0x624 down while +0x80c != 2 and +0x804 != 1. At 0 it writes +0x80c = 3 and raises a client error. Offline: OnGameFinish sets +0x80c = 1, nothing ever sets 2, and the state STALLS (blocking gate 2). RecvPreparingMissionEnd (+0xdd0, 0x1471cb7e0) handles a forced end when the message's member id equals the local id (0 offline): +0x804 = 2 (Finished) if msg+0x20 or msg+0x21 is set, else 1 (Aborted); it sets the notice flag +0x808, +0x538 = 4 and calls vf+0xab8.

findings.topic: States 16-17 WaitingIGCEndingStart, IGCEnding
findings.finding: State 16: Enter +0xd58 = 0x1471c8330 sets GM+0x754 = INI IGCENDING_SYNC_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 30) and fades. It calls local plane vf+0x970(1), sets input-block bytes +0x13b8..+0x13be and calls 0x147d505a0. Tick +0xd60 = 0x1471c8530 counts +0x754 down by dt. When CountAtLeast(NM+0x210, 0x10) >= MemberCount or the timeout reaches 0, it builds the local evaluation with 0x147455980(plane+0x16c8, GI, &tmp), stores it in NM+0xe0 (0x146e3a8e0), calls 0x147457450, sends EvaluationData through GM.NetworkObject 0x1474a6660 when that object exists, and calls NextState. State 17: Enter +0xd68 = nullsub. Tick +0xd70 = 0x1471c8750 uses sub-state +0x580. It waits while 0x147ecdfa0 is true. It clears the forced-end notice when +0x808 is set. When +0x804 == 1 (Aborted) it calls NextState at once. Otherwise it plays the ending IGC (finish delegate vtable 0x14cb37380, exit +0xd78 0x1471c8ac0 → NextState at 0x1471c8c60; sub-state 1 runs vf+0xbd0). Offline both work natively.

findings.topic: State 18 SyncEvaluation; EvaluationData / EvaluationList
findings.finding: Enter +0xd80 = 0x1471c8d70 is bookkeeping (0x4000) only. Tick +0xd88 = 0x1471c8e10 waits until CountAtLeast(0x12) >= MemberCount. It then takes UD = UserDataManager (GI+0x8e0, which is what 0x147ece300 returns), copies NM+0xe0 into UD+0x80+0x1b0, stores the plane+0x16c8 evaluation summary (0x147455730) in UD+0x80+0x200, and calls NextState. The EvaluationData handler 0x1474cf3c0 (SystemObject) keeps NM+0x90[member] and copies 13 ints and a byte into that member's plane at +0x1764..+0x17e9. EvaluationList (0x1474cf670) is factory-only, so the server makes it. Offline the state passes at once and only local data reaches the result.

findings.topic: State 19 Ended → Result map (ALiveResultAvatarGameMode, NetworkResultManager)
findings.finding: Enter +0xd90 = 0x1471c8f30 calls 0x147893e50(GI+0x908) and 0x14738ba60(world). If +0x804 == 1 it takes AbortPath 0x1471c5f70: clear NM+0x710/+0x718/+0x720, then 0x147ec9fc0(world), whose destination is unknown. Otherwise it calls +0xb18 = 0x1471c5d20: mode type 10 or 11 also aborts; otherwise it sets MapChange 0x147ece710()+0x1d5 = 1, stops 'AKE_Bgm_Online_AllMVP_Stop', sets the loading tip, and travels with 0x147901bf0(0x147ece5f0(world), &ResultMapReference GM+0x380). Last it calls NM 0x1474b5950(NM, 0). Tick +0xd98 = nullsub. The Result map's mode is ALiveResultAvatarGameMode (StaticClass 0x1480dbec0, size 0x428). Begin 0x1480f3d30 sets +0x420 = 1 and +0x424 = INI RESULT_START_SYNC_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 5). Tick 0x1480f3de0 first sets local ResultState NM+0x2b0[local] = 2 (sent online through 0x1474cdf20). It then waits until CountAtLeast(NM+0x2b0, 2) >= MemberCount or the timeout ends, then starts the result UI (PC→+0x980, 0x1475e23b0(…, 1)) and sets +0x420 = 3. Offline it passes at once. ULiveNetworkResultManager (GI+0x960, TMap<FString, ULiveNetworkResultObject*>) carries only the ResultEmote traffic (send 0x1474ca570 through 0x1474a2190, handler 0x1474ca710). The reward data (UserData+0xba8..+0xc18 and +0xc20) comes only from MissionRewardUser and LiveWebAPI, so offline it stays empty. What the result widgets do with no rewards, and whether they call LiveWebAPI themselves, is unknown because that UI code is protected.

findings.topic: Which end-of-match paths reach Bandai services
findings.finding: Senders that reach Strix are GameModeState, GameTime, PauseTime, TimeUp, PreparingMissionEnd, EvaluationData, ResultState and ResultEmote. All of them go through 0x1474a2190, which returns quietly with no Strix client (prior, verified), and most are also guarded by +0x1fa. The only paths that reach LiveWebAPI start from server-made messages: MissionRewardUser (handler 0x1474c8f80) → 0x1479bdc40 (request object UserData+0x1220; 0x1479297c0 caches GI.LiveWebAPI_ +0x970) → 0x1479b5da0 (UserData+0x10f0; gate 0x147926ce0 also caches LiveWebAPI_) → 0x14793ead0 (UserData+0x1348 save). 0x1471cbb20 only writes the LiveWebAPI_+0x1f8 flag. AbortPath's 0x147ec9fc0 has an unknown destination, possibly a lobby that reconnects. The result UI is unknown. EasyAntiCheatPeerData has a SystemObject handler (0x1474d0970) that offline never runs; I did not look further, as instructed.

findings.topic: What +0x1fa == 1 would arm (why to stay offline)
findings.finding: With StrixManager+0x1fa = 1 and no Strix client: MemberCount returns 0 and LocalMemberIdx returns 0, so IsHost is still true and the barriers still pass. However: (a) SyncStartMatch arms the NM+0x620 timeout → 'client error : mission start timeout' (0x2f514b) unless the phase gate is detoured. (b) GameTerminating arms the NM+0x624 timeout → +0x80c = 3, which blocks for ever, plus a client error, unless stage 2 is written in time. (c) The online Tick runs the per-plane presence check against the MissionRoomMemberManager AircraftSelectorMap (plane+0x2200 name, selector+0x28), so a plane not registered there takes the disconnect path 0x1471b75f0. (d) Every state Enter writes NM+0x710/+0x718 bookkeeping, NextState fills the GameModeState buffer, and other areas switch behaviour: object registration and the report-only TakeDamage branch. To use the native barriers for real, RVNG would also need MemberCount (0x1474b39e0) to return 2 and would have to inject the peer's states. All of this is avoidable offline.

rvngImplications: Stay offline. Never set ULiveStrixManager+0x1fa and never create the Strix client (global 0x14e4c5818). Then IsHost (0x1474b38d0) is true on both PCs, MemberCount (0x1474b39e0) is 0, and every count barrier (states 5, 7, 9, 11, 16 and 18, plus the Result map's ResultState sync) passes natively. Do not fake NM+0x538, which is the last FLiveMessageError code, not a member count.

Prerequisite (from earlier research): before loading PL_DM_00x, set the MissionID at UserDataManager(GI+0x8e0)+0xf38 to a DM row (160010 to 160060) so that mode type 0x147ec9d20 returns DM (3), not 10 or 11.

DETOUR 1 (required), phaseIndex gate 0x1471c1050 (2026-11-02 exe; prologue 'push rbx; sub rsp,0x50; call 0x143fb5420'). While an RVNG match is active, return true only when the local state +0x758 == 12 and the peer has reported state 12 over the P2P link. That replaces the server setting the room property phaseIndex >= 1 and is also RVNG's synchronized start: the host sends 'go' and both return true on the same frame. CallStartMatch then unpauses the clock (0x1471b9c90(GM,1,0)) on both PCs. Alternative: replace DM vtable slot 0x14c693718+0xd20 (SyncStartMatch Tick 0x1471c79e0) with a wrapper that calls NextState 0x1471c6150 on 'go'.

MEMORY WRITE 2 (required), PreparingMissionEnd stage. When state 15 (GameTerminating) begins, write the uint32 at GM+0x80c = 2. That is exactly what the server-driven delegate 0x1471d47c4 does. Detect the state by hooking SetState 0x1471c6020 with dl == 15, or by polling +0x758. GameTerminating then waits WaitingRadioInterval (GM+0x3cc, reflected float; write it to shorten the wait) and moves to 16. Do not pre-write 2 before OnGameFinish unless the PreparingMissionEnd send should be skipped too: 0x1471cb5e0 returns early when +0x80c >= 1. Never write 3, which blocks for ever.

Never inject server-only messages such as FLiveMessageMissionRewardUser, EvaluationList, RealTime or ResultState through the router 0x1474ef630. MissionRewardUser alone starts the LiveWebAPI chain (0x1479bdc40 on UserData+0x1220, then 0x1479b5da0 and 0x14793ead0). Optional safety net while an RVNG match is active: detour 0x1479297c0 (the request objects' 'bind GI.LiveWebAPI_ (+0x970)' step) to return false and log the caller, after first testing that it has no side effects.

Clock. The native clock is local and correct offline: FinishTime = post-BeginPlay time + GM+0x498 seconds, paused until CallStartMatch. To set the length deterministically, write the float GM+0x498 before the delegate 0x14dd876b8 runs 0x1471b5160 (for example in a hook on slot +0x390, 0x1471af690). Or rewrite FinishTime through vf+0xa78 (0x1471b9940 writes +0x4b8) while still paused, that is, before CallStartMatch. To mirror FLiveMessageGameTime, the host sends its remaining seconds (vf+0xa88, 0x1471b9a60) and the guest sets +0x4b8 = its own synced now + remaining x 1e7. Absolute ticks differ per PC (clk+0x18 is 0 offline), so send relative values only.

Ending. Time-up is local on each PC: vf+0xb30 → +0x538 = 2. VictoryScore needs mirrored scores (other area). For a forced end such as link loss or surrender, call RecvPreparingMissionEnd vf+0xdd0 (0x1471cb7e0) with member id 0 (the local id offline) and msg+0x20 or +0x21 set, which gives +0x804 = 2 (Finished) and +0x538 = 4. That keeps the result travel; avoid +0x804 = 1 (Aborted), because AbortPath 0x1471c5f70 → 0x147ec9fc0 has an unknown destination. GamePlaying ends by itself 3.0 s after OnGameFinish through ULiveOnlineMissionEndSequence, so no hook is needed there.

Results. Let Ended's +0xb18 (0x1471c5d20) travel to /Game/OnlineMode/Maps/Menu/Result. ALiveResultAvatarGameMode's sync (0x1480f3de0) passes offline. If the Result map hangs or shows broken reward panels, detour 0x1471c5d20 to RVNG's own summary or map. Optionally feed the opponent's evaluation summary into NM+0x90 or the opponent plane's +0x1764..+0x17e9 fields (as the EvaluationData handler 0x1474cf3c0 does) before SyncEvaluation copies NM+0xe0 into UserDataManager+0x80+0x1b0.

Optional 'mimic online barriers' mode, not needed for a working match: detour MemberCount 0x1474b39e0 to return 2, and write the peer's state into NM+0x210 with 0x1474cc910(NM+0x210, 1, state) whenever the peer reports a NextState (local key 0). Do the same on the Result map with NM+0x2b0 (peer = 2), and for IGC skips with NM+0x300. Every native sync point would then really wait for the opponent. It costs more hooks and touches more code that has never been exercised offline.
blockers: Nothing here has been seen in a real game log on this build: all of it is static RE. The Survival autotest logs contain no online-state strings.

0x1474cc700 (CountAtLeast) is a jump into protected .sbss code. The '>= N' meaning comes from its callers. The offline conclusions do not depend on it, because the comparison is against MemberCount == 0.

vf+0xaa8 (the MissionConfig apply, reached through 0x1471b9e80 → 0x15bde9600) and vf+0xa58 (0x1471b9900) are protected. That GM+0x498 receives MissionLimitTime (MC_DM 210 s) instead of keeping the ctor's 480 s is inferred, not proven.
phaseIndex as a ROOM (not member) property rests on the shape of the structs that the Strix wrappers 0x1452945a0 and 0x1452947b0 return. RVNG detours the gate anyway.
The Result screen's widgets and reward panels are protected UI code, so neither their behaviour without MissionRewardUser/WebAPI data nor any WebAPI calls they make could be determined.
AbortPath's destination 0x147ec9fc0 (calls 0x147ec9e40, 0x147206880, 0x14720c6f0) was not resolved; it may lead to an online lobby.
