The local IGCState write 0x1474ae770 happens on a later tick only while 0x147a59150()+0x60f is still set. Release needs CountAtLeast(NM+0x300,(GM+0x614<<8)|2) >= max(MemberCount,1) = 1 and IGC+0x90 != 0, so this barrier does depend on the protected CountAtLeast semantics.

A second state machine shares NM+0x210. 0x1471b9810 increments GM+0x578 (cap 0x1e), writes NM+0x210[memberId] = +0x578 with the same key and NetworkObject buffer as the online NextState, and enters via vf+0xa40. Any RVNG mirroring of NM+0x210 must account for which machine wrote the value.

The NM tick is 0x1474b94f0 (not 0x1474b9a43, which is a mid-function address) and is gated as a whole by NM+0x635. Besides NM+0x620/+0x624 it runs timers NM+0x610 (errors 0x2f4d67/0x2f4d63/0x2f514f/0x2f5150; picks 'aircraft select room connect failed' when NM+0x538 > 0), NM+0x614 ('aircraft information recv timeout', 0x2f5148), NM+0x618, NM+0x61c ('Random lottery timeout', online only), NM+0x628 and NM+0x630 (d_net.txt). Their offline arming points were not traced; add them to the runtime logger.
CountAtLeast's target 0x15c19a270 is readable TSet bit-array iteration with obfuscated constants (k_cnt.txt), so its '>= N' meaning can be confirmed statically or with one runtime log line.

The DM VictoryScore check 0x1471df5f0 runs on every PC (no host gate). It compares ULiveDeathMatchMissionConfig.VictoryScore (config+0x200, propoff) with 0x147d19600(plane) for each plane in world-mgr+0x138, then sets +0x538=3 (byte) and calls vf+0xab8. Mirrored scores therefore trigger the end locally on both PCs.

DM also overrides vtable slots +0xa30, +0xb40 (DM MissionConfig CDO fallback used by 0x1471b5920), +0xc40 (0x1471df740) and +0xc48. The vtables live in a read-only section named '.tls' (0x14ab04000, characteristics 0x40000040), so slot patches need VirtualProtect and would affect every class sharing the vtable entry. Inline detours are preferable.

0x1474b3860 (used by the GameTerminating tick to self-send PME) returns false statically whenever the Strix client global 0x14e4c5818 is null (0x1474b386e → 0x1474b38c6), so offline the state-15 stage is decided only by RVNG's +0x80c write (answers open question 6).

report.summary: Every address here is from the 2026-11-02 AceCombat8.exe (551,201,904 bytes, image base 0x140000000). Scratch dumps and scripts are in <scratchpad>/pvp_research/deep-wire/ (P below means that folder). FLiveMessages are Strix C++ SDK objects held in MSVC std::shared_ptr: {T* obj, control block*}. The control block keeps the strong count at +8 and the weak count at +0xC. A message's vtable slot 0 is GetMetaClass, slot 2 is the deleting destructor and slot 3 is ToString. The header is +0x8 TriggerTimeMs (actually 100 ns ticks of the synced clock), +0x10 NetworkTypeId (u8), +0x14 NetworkId (u32), then +0x18/+0x19 and +0x1C, which are not serialized (+0x1C is the sender, written by the router). The payload starts at +0x20. A network object N is a UObject: its Outer (N+0x20) is the owner, and N+0x28 is a u64 key, (ELiveNetworkType << 56) | id. Registering an object (slot 87 → base 0x1474a1b90) puts N into StrixManager+0x2E0 under that key. There is no online check, and if the key is already present the first entry stays. The router 0x1474ef630 looks the target up by (msg+0x10 << 56) | msg+0x14 and dispatches through N+0x38 by the class id at metaclass+0x48. The system object (key 1<<56) is created and registered at GameInstance init on every run, including offline. The game-mode object (key 6<<56) and the player-plane objects (2<<56 | id) are only created online, but RVNG can make all three plane steps happen itself offline. Offline, every plane would get id 0, so RVNG must assign the ids, before registration. The send function 0x1474a2190 ignores its first argument, takes the shared_ptr by value, and reaches Strix only through the client global 0x14e4c5818. RVNG should therefore replace it outright rather than chain to the original. The 'message too old' check is not a per-message drop. It is a disconnect rule in the NetworkManager tick: more than half the members with consecutive GameModeState delays over 15 s. It only runs while StrixManager+0x1F9 is set, and setting that flag without a live Strix client triggers an immediate 'Disconnected from the room server' error, so RVNG must leave +0x1F9 at 0. Best result: RVNG can ship any message as bytes with the game's own Strix serializer: MemoryStream + MessagePackEncoder → 0x14a3b13f0, and MessagePackDecoder → 0x1453bb4d0 returning a std::shared_ptr. The class registry is filled at GameInstance init, and class ids are SuperFastHash(class name), so they match on both PCs. Hand-marshalling is needed only as a fallback. The five extra senders belong to the lobby (ULiveAvatarManager, /Script/LiveLobby): AvatarCreation, AvatarAction, AvatarEmote, AvatarLocation and PlayerStatusUpdate. A deathmatch never uses them.

findings.topic: Build, tools and scratch evidence
Message object model and shared_ptr layout
findings.finding:
**Allocation and control block.**
- A message is created by a make_shared-style allocation: GMalloc (0x14e410280)->vf+0x28(size+0x10, align 16).
- The control block comes first: vtable 0x14bfd1c88, uses=1 at +8, weaks=1 at +0xC. The object follows at +0x10. Example: Damage, 0x1474bbec0.
- Control-block vtable 0x14bfd1c88 slots: [0] _Destroy 0x1453aeb90 calls obj->vf+0x10(0); [1] _Delete_this 0x1453aeb70; [2] 0x1453b7dc0.
- Objects that come out of the Strix deserializer use std::_Ref_count<strix::net::object::Object> instead (vtable 0x14af12de0, confirmed by RTTI). Its 0x18-byte block is {vt, uses, weaks, ptr}, and its [0] calls obj->vf+0x10(1).
- Release always works the same way: decrement +8; at 0 call ctl->vf0; then decrement +0xC; at 0 call ctl->vf1. This is the epilogue at 0x1474a22b1-0x1474a22de.

**Message vtable** (Damage 0x14bfd70d0): [0] GetMetaClass (0x14525a190 jumps to getter 0x1452b4240), [1] 0x14a3b04d0, [2] deleting destructor 0x14525b150 (frees the TArray at +0x38, base destructor 0x14a3b04c0, FMemory free), [3] ToString 0x14525ac10.

**Base object.** The Strix Object constructor 0x14a3b04b0 only sets the base vtable 0x14af0f160.

**Header fields.**
- Serialized: TriggerTimeMs u64 +0x8, NetworkTypeId u8 +0x10, NetworkId u32 +0x14 (FLiveMessageBase metaclass and ToString 0x145228920).
- Not serialized: +0x18 and +0x19 bytes, and +0x1C u32. make_shared zeroes them. The own-plane updater sets Physics+0x18=1 at 0x147d5e999. The router writes +0x1C.
- Classes derived from FLiveMessageLogOutput (FlightEngineInput, PostStallManeuver, FlightEngineHighGTurn, WeaponData, ElectronicMeasureData, ScoreData) have no header; their fields start at +0x8.

findings.topic: Network-object identity, router map, register and unregister
findings.finding:
**Layout.** N is a UObject. N+0x20 is UObject::OuterPrivate, the owner: the plane, the NetworkManager or the GameMode. N+0x28 is a u64 key = (ELiveNetworkType << 56) | id, so the type byte is N+0x2F. ELiveNetworkType values: 1 System, 2 Player, 3 Npc, 4 Bot, 5 Unit, 6 GameMode, 7 SimplePlayerResponse, 32 Lobby, 33 Guild, 34 Centurion.

**Register (base 0x1474a1b90**, called first by every slot-87 registration).
- It finds the GameInstance through World+0x1d8 and checks IsA ULiveGameInstance (0x146e2f590).
- In StrixManager (GI+0x910) +0x2E0, a TMap<u64, TWeakObjectPtr> with 0x18-byte elements, hash (key>>32)*23 + key, it adds {N+0x28, weak(N)} only if the key is absent.
- An existing key, even with a stale weak pointer, wins. There is no online test.

**Unregister.** 0x1474a1ab0 removes SM+0x2E0[N+0x28] (TMap::Remove 0x142800cf0). Callers include game-object teardown 0x147d14490 and GameMode 0x1471b62b0.

**Per-object handler map.** N+0x38 is a TMap<int32 classId, UE TSharedPtr<entry>> with 0x20-byte elements; the reference-controller vtable is 0x14cb66ca8.
- Entries are created by 0x1474a1d70, a 0x58-byte allocation: +0x00 send-delegate list, +0x18 receive multicast list, +0x30/+0x38 state-message shared_ptr, +0x40 flag, +0x50 interval in 100 ns ticks.
- Entries are filled by 0x1474a1e90 (handler) and 0x1474a1f10 (state slot).

findings.topic: Player-plane network object lifecycle and id assignment
findings.finding:
Plane vslots (ALivePlayerPlane vtable 0x14cbef168):

**+0xc60 = 0x147d5e650 (create).**
- If plane+0xed0 is 0, it calls NewObject<ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane>(class 0x146ef9b60, Outer=plane) through StaticConstructObject 0x141abec70 and stores the result at plane+0xed0.
- It has no online dependency, and Survival already runs it offline.

**+0xc58 = 0x147d5e5c0 (assign id).**
- Only if N+0x28 == 0: id = StrixManager+0x1fa ? 0x1474efb30(SM, NM+0x520) : 0.
- It writes plane+0x53b8 = id and N+0x28 = 0x0200000000000000 | id.
- 0x1474efb30 returns 0 when the Strix client 0x14e4c5818 is null, otherwise the first dword of the Strix room-member record from 0x1452947b0. So offline every plane gets key 0x0200000000000000.

**Remote copies** get their id in the remote spawn 0x1471b84f0:
- r14 = MissionRoomMemberManager 0x147492730(memberId);
- plane+0x53b8 = r14, N+0x28 = 2<<56 | r14 (0x1471b87c7), role +0xed8 = 2 (0x1471b87da).

**+0xc68 = 0x147d5e740 (register).**
- Calls N->vf+0x2b8. For a player plane that is 0x1474c34f0, which runs the GameObject registration 0x1474a7c70, which runs the base 0x1474a1b90.
- Then, if role != 2 (vf+0xc38), it tail-calls 0x1474c4380(N, plane+0x2268), which fills N+0x98 Physics from the flight engine.

**The plane's own state is refreshed every tick** by 0x147d5e790 (called at 0x147d53641). It needs N to be a ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane and role == 3 (vf+0xc40). It calls 0x1474c4380 (physics, the PSM/HighGTurn arrays, the synced time). When the input changes, it copies the input into N+0x170 and appends a FlightEngineInput (vtable 0x14bfd7e50, 0x28 bytes) to Physics+0x70, then sets Physics+0x8 = synced now and Physics+0x18 = 1.

**Order and offline use.**
- In the game the setup chunk 0x147d13de3 runs create → id → register only when StrixManager+0x1fa is set (prior research).
- Called offline: create and register work, because nothing in 0x1474a1b90 or 0x1474a7c70 tests an online flag. The id must be written before register: registration stamps the state-slot messages with N+0x28 (0x1474a1f6b), and the map key is taken at registration time.
sources: E:/ACE8 Survival Mode/runtime/flight_coop2mp.c:18-26 (Survival writes N+0x98 / N+0x170, verified in game)

findings.topic: Game-mode network object (ALiveGameMode+0x738)
findings.finding:
**Creation.**
- ALiveGameMode::BeginPlay-like 0x1471b5920 tests StrixManager+0x1fa at 0x1471b59b3. Only when it is set does it call vf+0xc48, write GM+0x738->+0x28 = 0x0600000000000000 (constant, 0x1471b59d8) and call vf+0xc50.
- For ALiveSoloPVPGameMode (vtable 0x14ca32fe8): +0xc48 = 0x1471b0ce0, which jumps to 0x1471cc030 = NewObject<ULiveNetworkGameMode>(class 0x146ef7e70, Outer=GM) stored at GM+0x738. +0xc50 = 0x1471b08e0 = GM+0x738->vf+0x2b8, which is registration 0x1474a5730. The base ALiveGameMode +0xc48 is an empty stub.
- A PVPVE variant 0x1471e1490 creates ULiveNetworkPVPVEGameMode (class 0x146ef9e60).
- There is no ULiveNetworkDeathMatchGameMode.

**What it receives:** PhaseStart, PhaseClear, MissionClear, MissionEnd 0x1474a6fa0, EmergencyMissionClear, TeamScoreAddition 0x1474a70a0, AIActionEventExecute, and ExplosiveWeaponHit (thunk 0x1474a73d0).

**Offline:** the object does not exist, so the ExplosiveWeaponHit sender wrapper 0x147f25e10 (it needs GM+0x738) never sends.

findings.topic: System network object (ULiveNetworkManager+0x4c0)
findings.finding:
**Creation, offline included.**
- GameInstance init (chunk 0x1478c9ac1) creates ULiveNetworkManager (class 0x146ef8de0) into GI+0x928 and immediately calls 0x1474acd50(NM) at 0x1478ca4ef.
- 0x1474acd50 creates ULiveNetworkSystemObject (class 0x146ef8d30, Outer=NM) into NM+0x4c0, sets N+0x28 = 0x0100000000000000 (0x1474ace05) and calls vf+0x2b8 (registration 0x1474ccc30) without any online test.
- The message-class registry 0x145295560 is also called from the same GameInstance init (0x1478ca243).

**Consequences.** The system object (key System<<56 | 0) is in StrixManager+0x2e0 in every session. Because its key is identical on both PCs, a peer's system messages route to the local system object. Its owner check uses N+0x20 = NM (0x146ef8de0).

**Do not register it a second time.** 0x1474a1d70 allocates a new entry on every call; whether the TMap add replaces the old entry or duplicates the handler was not traced.

findings.topic: State slots (periodic state messages) and the nested flight-state arrays
findings.finding:
**GameObject slots** are registered by 0x1474a7c70 through 0x1474a1f10, but only if the Outer IsA ALiveGameObject (0x146d0dee0) and Outer->vf+0xaa0 (IsPlayerPlane) is true. Each row is slot, message, interval, send callback, receive callback:
- N+0x88 PhysicsOld, 80 ms, 0x1474a8bd0, 0x1474a9e70
- N+0x98 Physics, 80 ms, 0x1474a8d90, 0x1474aa1c0
- N+0xb8 AirCurrentStates, 80 ms, 0x1474a8e70, 0x1474aa400
- N+0xc8 AIPhysicsOld, 160 ms, 0x1474a8cb0, 0x1474aa020
- N+0xd8 AIPhysics, 160 ms, 0x1474a8fb0, 0x1474aa540
- N+0xe8 AIAirCurrentStates, 160 ms, 0x1474a9110, 0x1474aa6c0
- N+0xf8 Health, 500 ms, 0x1474a9250, 0x1474aa800

**SystemObject slots** (0x1474ccc30):
- SysObj+0x88 GameModeState, 10,000 ms (heartbeat), receive 0x1474cefb0
- SysObj+0x98 PhaseState, 1000 ms, receive 0x1474cf250

**How a slot works.**
- 0x1474a1f10 stamps the slot message once at registration and stores interval × 10000 (100 ns ticks) at entry+0x50.
- A send callback such as Physics 0x1474a8d90 copies *(N+0x98) into a new make_shared message (copy constructor 0x1474bf7f0, 0x80 bytes) and sends it without restamping.
- The Physics receive callback 0x1474aa1c0 runs only for an ALivePlayerPlane Outer: it calls the NetworkCheatManager check 0x1474a3f20, then copies the whole incoming message (header, +0x18, +0x19, +0x1c, payload, arrays) into *(N+0x98).

**Physics carries the sub-states.** There is no slot for N+0xa8 PostStallManeuver. Physics+0x50 is TArray<PostStallManeuver> (0x38-byte stride, vtable 0x14bfd7e30, copied from N+0x140), +0x60 is TArray<FlightEngineHighGTurn> (0x28, vtable 0x14bfd7e70, from N+0x150), +0x70 is TArray<FlightEngineInput> (0x28, vtable 0x14bfd7e50, from N+0x170).

**Unknown:** the timer that calls send callbacks every entry+0x50 was not found. Base-object vtable slot 88 (0x146ef8bd0) jumps into the protected section (0x15a0cb740).

findings.topic: Plane event senders: what lets them fire
findings.finding:
The plane-side wrappers in the 0x147d608xx-0x147d615xx cluster call the message builders only if three things hold: plane+0xed0 is non-null, it IsA ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane (0x146ef9b60), and plane->vf+0xc40 (role == 3) is true. Example: LockedTarget, 0x147d60863-0x147d608bb.

The builders themselves do not test StrixManager+0x1fa. ExplosiveWeaponFire is built inline in the weapons-fired fragment 0x147d60d48-0x147d61228 (stamp 0x147d611f5, send 0x147d61216; WeaponData elements are 0x50 bytes).

ExplosiveWeaponHit goes through 0x147f25e10(weapon, -, bHit). It needs weapon+0x368->vf+0xc40 (the launcher's role == 3), the authority GameMode and GM+0x738, and then calls 0x1474a6b10(GM-NO, weapon+0x6e8 WeaponNetworkId, bHit).

So offline, a plane with role 3 and a registered N produces its own outgoing gameplay messages. They reach 0x1474a2190 and stop there.

findings.topic: Send contract 0x1474a2190 and the Strix path behind it
findings.finding:
**Signature:** void Send(void* rcx_unused, std::shared_ptr<FLiveMessageBase>* byValue).
- rcx is never read; callers pass N, but the identity comes only from the stamp.
- The callee releases [rdx+8] at 0x1474a22b1, so the caller hands over its copy.

**Body.**
- If the Strix client global 0x14e4c5818 is null, it only releases the pointer and returns.
- Otherwise it searches client+0x60 (a std::map<int, shared_ptr<ctx>>) for key 0. If found, it calls 0x14a4379a0(ctx, dl=1, &msgCopy, &opts, &emptyFn, &emptyFn), which reaches ctx->vf+0x2c8 (the Strix room relay request, inferred).

**All sends go through it.** sendmap.py found 84 caller functions. Standard pattern: make_shared → Stamp(N, copy) → fill payload → Send(N, copy). A sender's two calls are only the allocation-success and allocation-failure paths.

**The other send** 0x1474a2300(N, int, shared_ptr) uses 0x1452949d0 (member lookup) and 0x1474a2560. Its only caller is 0x14813e6cf, in the LiveLobby cluster (Centurion/Avatar, inferred).

findings.topic: Stamp 0x1474a1c90 and the synced clock
findings.finding:
**Stamp(N, shared_ptr byValue)** writes msg+0x10 = N+0x2f, msg+0x14 = (u32)N+0x28 and msg+0x8 = synced now, then releases its copy.

**Synced now** = 0x147907660() + c[0x18] − c[0x8] + c[0x20], with c = 0x147907550() (lazy singleton 0x14e5101b8).
- 0x147907660 computes (QPC × SecondsPerCycle + 16777216.0) × 1e7, so the unit is 100 ns despite the field name TriggerTimeMs.
- Receivers convert ages with 1e-7 (constant 0x14d292d6c).
- c[0x20] is set by the RealTime handler (deep-sync / deep-server).

findings.topic: Router 0x1474ef630 contract and the Strix receive lambda
findings.finding:
**Signature:** void Router(ULiveStrixManager* SM, const std::shared_ptr<UID>* sender, const std::shared_ptr<Object>* msg). Both pointers are borrowed: the router takes and releases its own references.

**Steps.**
1. Calls SM->vf+0x188 (GetWorld).
2. If msg IsA FLiveMessageBase (getter 0x1452b79e0, IsA 0x14a3b0550 = Object::GetMetaClass + MetaClass::IsA 0x14a3c1820), it sets msg+0x1c = sender ? *(u32*)(sender.ptr+8) : 0.
3. If msg IsA NpcRandomLotteryResult (0x1452b5300), it forces msg+0x10 = 1.
4. key = (msg+0x10 << 56) | msg+0x14, looked up in SM+0x2e0.
5. Found and the weak pointer is valid (0x142606110 = stale test, 0x141ad95e0 = Get): classId = msg->vf0()->+0x48 is looked up in N+0x38. A hit broadcasts through 0x1474bb510 (iterates the invocation list backwards and calls each delegate's vf+0x60 with a shared_ptr copy). A miss is silently ignored.
6. Not found (or stale): if msg IsA Damage, the NM fallback runs.
7. If msg is not a FLiveMessageBase but IsA FLiveMessageError (0x1452afdc0), NM 0x1474b9080 runs.

**Strix entry.** Lambda 0x14750b2d0 (vtables 0x14cb6a9b8 room relay and 0x14cb6aa18 direct relay, bound by 0x1474eee50) calls Router(SM=[this+8], &notif+0x8, &notif+0x20). In the notification, +0x8/+0x10 is the sender shared_ptr (likely the member UID) and +0x20/+0x28 is the message shared_ptr.

In the handler ranges checked (0x1474aa990-0x1474ac000, 0x1474c6b30-0x1474c9100, 0x1474cefb0-0x1474d1650, 0x1474a6c80-0x1474a7630), no handler reads msg+0x1c.
sources: grep of handler ranges for '+ 0x1c]' reads

findings.topic: Fallbacks for messages with no target object
findings.finding:
**Unrouted Damage.** 0x1474b8a50 (thunk) appends the shared_ptr to the TArray at NM+0x5b8.
- The NetworkManager tick calls 0x1474b8740 at 0x1474ad598, before any online test.
- 0x1474b8740 retries every queued Damage: it looks up the target, and once the target exists and IsA ALiveGameObject it calls the Damage handler 0x1474aa990, then removes the entry.
- So a Damage that arrives before its target is registered is delayed, not lost.

**FLiveMessageError.** 0x1474b9080 logs it (0x1474b5650) and calls the error handler 0x1474b9280.

findings.topic: 'Received message was too old': a disconnect rule, not a per-message drop
findings.finding:
**What happens each tick.** In the NetworkManager tick (chunk 0x1474ad57e/0x1474ad641):
- esi = MemberCount (0x1474b39e0).
- If StrixManager+0x1f9 == 0, the whole block is skipped (0x1474ad63b).
- If +0x1f9 == 1: when SM+0x28 is null, or the Strix client 0x14e4c5818 is null, or client+0x50[NM+0x520] fails 0x14a44c700, it clears word SM+0x1f9 (both +0x1f9 and +0x1fa) and raises 'Disconnected from the room server'. The code is 0x2f4d61, 0x2f4d66 or 0x2f5151, chosen by NM+0x53c.
- If still connected and +0x1fa is set: when members <= 0 it raises 0x2f4d64 'number of room member is 0'.
- When 0x1474ba280(NM) returns false it raises 0x2f4d65: UTF-16 'ULiveNetworkManager::Tick : received message was too old' (0x14cb67ec0) and 'client error : ...' (0x14cb67f40).
- The error path marks 0x147ece4d0(...)+0x28 |= 0x80 and calls 0x1474b8e70 (error dialog / leave).

**The test.** 0x1474ba280 returns true when members <= 0. Otherwise it counts entries of NM+0x6a8 (TMap<int32 member, int32 lateCount>) whose value is > 0, and returns count <= (int)((members+1) × 0.5) (constant 0x14d293748 = 0.5).

**Who fills NM+0x6a8.** Only the GameModeState handler 0x1474cefb0. While GM vf+0xb70 is true, age = (now − msg+0x8) × 1e-7 s. If age > NM+0x6f8 the member's counter is incremented, otherwise reset to 0.
- NM+0x6f8 defaults to 15.0 (0x1474acaed) and is overwritten from InformationManager parameter 0x1e (0x1474ad46c-0x1474ad4a5).

findings.topic: The five extra senders 0x14813a280/570/750/930/ab60
findings.finding:
All five are lobby (hub avatar) senders. They stamp, then send with the network object at ULiveAvatarManager+0xb8.
- ULiveAvatarManager is a UGameInstanceSubsystem from /Script/LiveLobby. 0x148108250 = GetSubsystem with StaticClass 0x1480b4e20, names 0x14cc2447a and 0x14cc23540.
- 0x14813a280 builds AvatarCreation (make_shared 0x1453a5fa0, vtable 0x14bfd76b0, 0x58 bytes; caller 0x1480ed267).
- 0x14813a570 builds AvatarAction (0x1453a6150, vtable 0x14bfd75f0; caller 0x148119b85).
- 0x14813a750 builds AvatarEmote (0x1453a6080, vtable 0x14bfd7630; callers 0x148119b24 and 0x148119b6d).
- 0x14813a930 builds AvatarLocation (0x1453a5b90, vtable 0x14bfd76d0; caller 0x1481185c1).
- 0x14813ab60 builds PlayerStatusUpdate (0x1453a5c60, vtable 0x14bfd6d78; caller 0x148100bb1).
- Gate: (NM+0x4c9 || SM+0x1fa) and SM+0x30 in {1,2}.

A deathmatch never uses them; RVNG should drop them.

findings.topic: How Strix serializes an FLiveMessage
findings.finding:
**Type info.** Each class has a static MetaClass.
- Its getter (for example 0x1452b4240 for Damage) lazily runs an init (0x145301f40) that builds the metaclass (vtable 0x14bfd5008).
- The init sets metaclass+0x48 = 0x14a3b0810(class name). That function is Paul Hsieh's SuperFastHash, so the id is deterministic and identical on both PCs.
- The id is registered with 0x14a3c1890 in the registry std::map<int, MetaClass*> (0x14a3c1640()+0x10). 0x14a3c15e0(classId) looks a MetaClass up by id.
- Fields are added with AddField 0x14520c9c0.
- Metaclass vtable slot 3 (+0x18) = Create, which allocates the object with GMalloc and constructs it (Damage 0x1452b41b0, DamageClient 0x1452b40d0; others in create_sizes.txt). Slot 4 returns the metaclass.
- GameInstance init calls the registry function 0x145295560, which touches all 146 getters, so every class can be (de)serialized offline.

**Serializer manager.** 0x14a3c1090 is a lazy singleton (0x14dea3188; DefaultSerializationManager, ctor 0x14a3da710, vtable 0x14af12688). vf+0x20 0x14a3de600 serializes and vf+0x28 0x14a3db8b0 deserializes.

**Entry points.**
- Serialize(_, Encoder*, MetaClass*, Object*) = 0x14a3b13f0.
- Deserialize(_, Decoder*, MetaClass* declared, Object** out) = 0x14a3b1240.
- shared_ptr variant: 0x1453bb4d0(_, Decoder*, std::shared_ptr<Object>* out) passes the declared Object metaclass 0x1452c3960, then wraps the raw result in std::_Ref_count<Object> (vtable 0x14af12de0).
- The relay's nested-message field serializer, DynamicSerializerImpl<shared_ptr<Object>> (vtable 0x14af15818), calls exactly these: slot 1 0x1453b5c30 → 0x14a3b13f0, slot 2 0x1453b5bd0 → 0x1453bb4d0.

**Wire format** (MessagePackEncoder, vtable 0x14af14b90, 0x18 bytes: +8 Stream*, +0x10 ok flag):
- object header: vf+0x68 0x14a403760 writes D6 <tag> <classId as BE32>, a msgpack fixext4;
- then vf+0x88 0x14a4032e0 writes an array header (field count);
- then the fields in metaclass order (positional; the BeginField/EndField slots +0x78/+0x80 are no-ops);
- type tags 0x0f and 0x15 add extra class-id data (0x14a3de7ae-0x14a3de87d).
The deserializer reads the tag and header, finds the metaclass by id (0x14a3dbce2) and instantiates it.

findings.topic: Calling the game's own serializer: recipe (template: DefaultMessageChannel::Send 0x14a3f59d0 and Adapter::Receive 0x14a3f3680)
findings.finding:
**Encode (MemoryStream object: 0x28 bytes, vtable 0x14af14a78, std::vector at +0x8/+0x10/+0x18, position at +0x20):**
1. ms: 0x14a402db0(ms, 0x800), then *(u64*)(ms+0x20) = 0.
2. enc[0x18] = {0}; 0x14a403250(enc); *(void**)(enc+8) = ms.
3. mc = msg->vf0().
4. ok = 0x14a3b13f0(&scratch, enc, mc, msg) && enc[0x10].
5. The bytes are [*(u8**)(ms+8), *(u8**)(ms+0x10)).
6. 0x14a402e20(ms, 0) frees the buffer but not ms.
The game's channel adds a 4-byte big-endian length prefix (0x14a3f5d94, 0x14a3f5dfa); RVNG does not need it.

**Decode:**
1. ms: 0x14a402db0(ms, len); write the bytes with vf+0x10 0x14a402f10(ms, data, len); set *(u64*)(ms+0x20) = 0.
2. dec[0x28] = {0}; 0x14a404570(dec) (it inits +8/+0x14/+0x18 and sets word +0x20 = 0x100); *(void**)(dec+8) = ms.
3. sp = {0,0}; ok = 0x1453bb4d0(&scratch, dec, &sp).
4. Clean up with 0x14a4045e0(dec, 0) and 0x14a402e20(ms, 0).

**Notes.**
- Allocation goes through UE's GMalloc (0x14e410280; vf+0x28 Malloc, vf+0x48 Free; operator new 0x14738d9e0).
- The non-serialized +0x18, +0x19 and +0x1c come out as 0.
- Run it on the game thread.
- No step touches the network. The only Strix side effects are the lazy singletons and the logger 0x14a3b0be0.

findings.topic: Cheat-report and EAC-related call sites RVNG must keep unreached
findings.finding:
**Receive-side checks.** The Physics receive (0x1474aa1c0 → 0x1474a3f20) and the Instant/Bullet weapon handlers (0x1474a43e0, 0x1474a48c0) call the NetworkCheatManager, reached through 0x147ece8b0(world) from GI.

**Reporting.** They report through NM 0x1474b8bb0. That function acts only when StrixManager+0x1fa is set: it calls the SystemObject Cheat sender 0x1474cecc0 (FLiveMessageCheat {CheatType, CheatMemberId, CheatTimeStamp, ReportMemberId}) and then the MissionRoomMemberManager path 0x147492510.

**Messages to block.**
- KickPlayer (handler 0x1474d0ee0, sender chunk 0x1474cee50).
- EasyAntiCheatPeerData (SystemObject handler 0x1474d0970, sender chunk 0x1474ce9e7). These are the game's own call sites only; nothing on the anti-cheat side was analysed.

All of these leave through 0x1474a2190.

rvngImplications:
Replace 0x1474a2190 completely (native detour; do not chain to the original). In the detour:
1. Read msg = *(void**)rdx and ctl = *(void**)(rdx+8).
2. Classify the message with IsA 0x14a3b0550(msg, getter()) or with its vtable.
3. Drop Cheat, KickPlayer, EasyAntiCheatPeerData, LatencyCheck, Error, Avatar*, PlayerStatusUpdate, Guild* and Centurion*.
4. Serialize everything else synchronously (next item) and queue the bytes for the P2P link.
5. Release the by-value reference exactly as the original epilogue at 0x1474a22b1 does: decrement ctl+8; at 0 call ctl->vf0; then decrement ctl+0xc; at 0 call ctl->vf1.
This keeps 0x14a4379a0 and the Strix client 0x14e4c5818 unreachable even if that global were ever non-null.

Serialize, on the game thread:
1. MemoryStream ms[0x28]: 0x14a402db0(ms, 0x800), then *(u64*)(ms+0x20) = 0.
2. MessagePackEncoder enc[0x18] = {0}: 0x14a403250(enc), then *(void**)(enc+8) = ms.
3. ok = 0x14a3b13f0(&tmp, enc, msg->vf0(), msg) && enc[0x10].
4. Send the bytes [*(u8**)(ms+8), *(u8**)(ms+0x10)).
5. Call 0x14a402e20(ms, 0).

Deserialize on the receiving PC, on the game thread:
1. ms: 0x14a402db0(ms, len); 0x14a402f10(ms, data, len); *(u64*)(ms+0x20) = 0.
2. dec[0x28] = {0}: 0x14a404570(dec), then *(void**)(dec+8) = ms.
3. std::shared_ptr sp = {0,0}; ok = 0x1453bb4d0(&tmp, dec, &sp).
4. Clean up: 0x14a4045e0(dec, 0) and 0x14a402e20(ms, 0).

Inject with Router 0x1474ef630(SM = GameInstance+0x910, &sender, &sp):
- sender = {&fakeUid, nullptr}, where fakeUid is any 16 bytes with the peer's member number as a u32 at +8. The router copies it into msg+0x1c.
- The router borrows both pointers. Release sp afterwards with the same sequence as the send detour.
- If the latency matters, restamp sp+0x8 first with the receiver's synced now: 0x147907660() + c[0x18] − c[0x8] + c[0x20], with c = 0x147907550().

Give each plane a unique id: offline, +0xc58 produces 0 for every plane.
- Own plane P: call vf+0xc60 (0x147d5e650). Write *(u64*)(P+0xed0 → +0x28) = 0x0200000000000000 | myNum and *(u32*)(P+0x53b8) = myNum. Set P+0xed8 = 3, which the role==3 senders and the input recorder 0x147d5e790 need. Then call vf+0xc68 (0x147d5e740) exactly once. +0xc58 can be skipped, or called: it no longer changes a non-zero N+0x28.
- Remote copy R: role 2, vf+0xc60, N+0x28 = 2<<56 | peerNum, R+0x53b8 = peerNum, then vf+0xc68.
- Use the same two numbers on both PCs. Never change N+0x28 after registration: registration stamps the state slots and keys StrixManager+0x2e0.
- Before re-registering a key, call Unregister 0x1474a1ab0(N), because the first entry wins.

Create the game-mode object offline after BeginPlay (0x1471b5920 skips it because StrixManager+0x1fa is 0): gm->vf+0xc48 (0x1471b0ce0 → 0x1471cc030), then *(u64*)(gm+0x738 → +0x28) = 0x0600000000000000, then gm->vf+0xc50 (0x1471b08e0). This enables the ExplosiveWeaponHit send/receive (0x147f25e10 / 0x1474a73d0) and the PhaseStart/MissionEnd/TeamScoreAddition handlers.
Do not create or re-register the system object (NM+0x4c0, key 1<<56). It already exists offline, and system messages from the peer route to it automatically because the key is the same on both PCs.

Leave StrixManager+0x1f9 at 0 at all times. Set with no Strix client, the NetworkManager tick clears +0x1f9/+0x1fa and raises 'Disconnected from the room server' (0x1474ad748 → 0x1474b8e70). With +0x1f9 = 0, the member-count and 'too old' rules (0x1474ba280, NM+0x6a8) never run. Keep +0x1fa at 0 too unless another area needs it: when +0x1fa is 1, the cheat-report path 0x1474b8bb0 becomes active.

For the messages the server makes (DamageClient, ScoreUpdate, RealTime, EvaluationList, LatencyResponse, RequestRespawn, RequestTeleportToRespawnPoint), the RVNG host either builds them or deserializes host-made bytes:
1. obj = metaclass Create, which is metaclass vtable slot +0x18 (DamageClient 0x1452b40d0, ScoreUpdate 0x1452b2c50, RealTime 0x1452b5b70, EvaluationList 0x1452b5e10, LatencyResponse 0x1452b4fd0; the rest in create_sizes.txt).
2. Wrap it with GMalloc(0x18) as {vt 0x14af12de0, 1, 1, obj}.
3. Fill msg+0x10/+0x14 with the target object's key and the payload. Allocate TArray memory through GMalloc 0x14e410280 (elements start with their vtable, e.g. ScoreData 0x14bfd7bf0).
4. Route it, or serialize it and ship it to the peer.

State traffic: the own plane's N+0x98/+0x170 state is filled by the game (0x147d5e790 / 0x1474c4380, role 3). If the periodic send pump does not run offline, RVNG must call the send callbacks itself: Physics 0x1474a8d90 every 80 ms, AirCurrentStates 0x1474a8e70 every 80 ms, Health 0x1474a9250 every 500 ms, all with rcx = N. GameModeState goes out every 10 s, and PhaseState every 1 s.

When RVNG injects a large Physics position jump (respawn or teleport) on the copy, the receiver runs the NetworkCheatManager check 0x1474a3f20. Offline it cannot report, because 0x1474b8bb0 needs +0x1fa. Even so, any Cheat or KickPlayer message that reaches the send detour must be dropped, never forwarded.
blockers: The timer that calls state-slot send callbacks every entry+0x50 interval was not found statically. Base-object vtable slot 88 (0x146ef8bd0) jumps into the virtualized .sbss code (0x15a0cb740). So it is unknown whether Physics, AirCurrentStates and Health are sent offline without RVNG calling 0x1474a8d90, 0x1474a8e70 and 0x1474a9250 itself.

Server-made messages (DamageClient, ScoreUpdate, RealTime, EvaluationList, LatencyResponse) have no client builder, so RVNG must construct them. The rules for when and what to send are in the server report. The element layouts of EvaluationList (EvaluationUsersList) and of EvaluationData's inline EvaluationAccumulateData have no resolved field names.

Metaclass registrations of a few classes (Health, PushFlare, EscapeInClouds, RealTime, AIInfo) run in protected code (0x1544c...). Their ToString writers and sizes were readable, and Health's field was too, but the exact serialized field order for those classes comes from the ToString writers, not from their AddField lists.

It was not traced whether re-running slot 87 (vf+0x2b8) on one object replaces or duplicates handler entries (0x1474a1d70 always allocates a new entry; how the TMap add 0x141fb4330 handles an existing key was not traced). Keep registration to exactly one call per object.
Ruled out by the hard boundaries: EasyAntiCheatPeerData (handler 0x1474d0970, sender chunk 0x1474ce9e7) is listed only as a game call site to drop. It was not analysed further.
openQuestions:
Serializer round trip, offline, modded, one PC:
1. In the 0x1474a2190 detour (or after building a Damage with Create 0x1452b41b0), serialize it with the recipe and log the byte count and the first 16 bytes. Expect D6 0F followed by the class id in big-endian.
2. Deserialize the bytes and compare the two objects' ToString (vtable slot 3) output.
3. Log *(void**)0x14e4c5818 at the same moment to confirm the Strix client is null offline.

Class-id agreement across PCs: on both PCs log *(u32*)(getter()+0x48) for Damage 0x1452b4240, Physics 0x1452b6f50, GameModeState 0x1452b63b0, ScoreUpdate 0x1452b2cd0 and ExplosiveWeaponFire 0x1452b7710. The values must be identical.

Offline registration:
1. For your own plane, set N+0x28 = 2<<56|1, P+0x53b8 = 1 and role 3, then call vf+0xc60/+0xc68.
2. Dump StrixManager+0x2e0 (count at +0x2e8, elements {u64 key, weak ptr, next}) and the N+0x38 count at +0x40. Expect the keys 0x0100000000000000 (system), 0x0200000000000001, and 0x0600000000000000 if you created the game-mode object.
3. Hook 0x1474a8d90, 0x1474a8e70 and 0x1474a9250 for 10 s. About 125, 125 and 20 calls means the pump runs offline; 0 means RVNG must pump.

Router loopback on one PC:
1. Spawn a role-2 copy registered as 2<<56|2.
2. In the send detour, copy each outgoing own-plane message through serialize and deserialize, rewrite msg+0x14 = 2, and inject it with Router(GI+0x910, {&uid{,2}, 0}, &sp).

checks.claim: RVNG implication / blocker: the periodic slot timer was not found, so RVNG may have to call 0x1474a8d90, 0x1474a8e70 and 0x1474a9250 itself every 80/80/500 ms. GameModeState goes out every 10 s and PhaseState every 1 s.
checks.evidence: The pump chain is 0x1478cccd0 (GI ticker, bound at 0x1478cb84e) → 0x1478ccd67 → 0x1474efd50(SM) → 0x1474a2770(N) → 0x14748d530(entry). It has no online-flag test. In online_gm.txt, SetState chunks 0x1471c61d5, 0x1471b9895 and 0x1471c6edd write SysObj+0x88 (+0x20 id, +0x24 state, +0x19=1) only when SM+0x1fa is set.

Slots are sent only when dirty (+0x18), when urgent (+0x19, which bypasses the interval) or when entry+0x40 is set, so they are not unconditional heartbeats. Offline, GameModeState is never filled or flagged; RVNG must fill SysObj+0x88 (+0x20 its member id, +0x24 state, +0x19=1) or synthesize the message. PhaseState's fill path was not traced. Who dirties Health was not traced.

checks.claim: RVNG implication: an injected large Physics jump runs the cheat check, but offline it cannot report, because 0x1474b8bb0 needs +0x1fa.
checks.evidence: 0x1474a3f20 has no +0x1fa test (cheatchk.txt), and on a speed violation it calls 0x1474b8bb0(NM, id=msg+0x14, type 3) at 0x1474a4177. 0x1474b8bb0 sends Cheat unconditionally (0x1474b8c18).
checks.correction: Offline, a respawn or teleport jump on a copy produces a FLiveMessageCheat (type 3, client_player_location) at the Send detour and is recorded in the NetworkCheatManager (0x1474a3430). Drop it in the detour. To avoid the record as well, set the copy's plane+0x8b1=1 before injecting a teleport; that is the one-shot skip consumed at 0x1474a3f9e. No writer of +0x8b1 exists in .text (batch3.txt), so the game's own setter is unknown and may be in protected code or reflection.

missed: The state-slot pump exists and runs offline. ULiveGameInstance binds ticker 0x1478cccd0 at GI init (lea at 0x1478cb84e). If GI+0x910 is non-null it calls 0x1474efd50(SM) (0x1478ccd67), which calls 0x1474a2770(N) for every valid object in SM+0x2e0, which calls 0x14748d530(entry) for every N+0x38 entry. 0x14748d530 sends when the interval (+0x50, 100 ns) has passed since the last send (+0x48) and any of entry+0x40, msg+0x18 (dirty) or msg+0x19 (urgent) is set. Within the interval it sends only if msg+0x19 is set. After sending it clears msg+0x18/+0x19 and sets +0x48 = now. This settles the report's main blocker. Static (AceCombat8.exe 2026-11-02; deep-wire-verify/pump.txt, pump_entry.txt, gi.txt).

The header bytes +0x18 and +0x19 are the slot's dirty and urgent flags. Own-plane Physics is dirtied on every tick by 0x1474c4380 (0x1474c4a5e) and by 0x147d5e790 (0x147d5e999). AirCurrentStates N+0x160 is dirtied at 0x1474c4ba4. The SysObj GameModeState gets +0x19=1 from SetState.

Offline, GameModeState never goes out. The online game-mode SetState chunks (0x1471b9895, 0x1471c61d5, 0x1471c6edd) always update the local member table NM+0x210 through 0x1474cc910 (member id 0 offline). They fill SysObj+0x88 (+0x20 SenderMemberId, +0x24 state) and set +0x19=1 only when SM+0x1fa is set. RVNG must fill that slot itself or synthesize GameModeState.

The GameModeState handler 0x1474cefb0 keys everything on the payload SenderMemberId (msg+0x20), not the router's msg+0x1c. It calls 0x1474cc910(NM+0x210, SenderMemberId, state), which feeds the peer-state table used by the Sync* gates, then 0x1474ba1f0(NM, SenderMemberId, RTT), then the NM+0x6a8 late counter. It also requires N->Outer IsA ULiveNetworkManager (0x146ef8de0). RVNG must put the peer's member id in SenderMemberId (static, gms_recv.txt).

The router silently drops messages for a key that is present but whose weak pointer is invalid (0x142606110 → `jne 0x1474efa3f`), including Damage, which then never reaches the NM+0x5b8 retry queue. Combined with 'first entry wins', a destroyed but not unregistered copy blackholes its id.

Offline, NetworkManager 0x1474b8bb0 sends FLiveMessageCheat (0x1474cecc0, vt 0x14bfd72b0, no online gate) whenever the system object exists. The Physics speed check 0x1474a3f20 raises cheat type 3 (client_player_location; ELiveNetworkCheatType.h) when distance² divided by the squared msg+0x8 delta exceeds a speed limit. plane+0x8b1 is a one-shot skip that 0x1474a3f9e clears; its setter is not in .text. 0x14710a230(world)+0x90 non-null disables the check. A zero timestamp delta makes the divisor 0, so any position change is reported. The KickPlayer send in cheat manager 0x1474a3430 is gated on +0x1fa (0x1474a3742) and 0x1474b3860. In-game test: inject a 5 km jump into a copy, with and without plane+0x8b1=1, and log what reaches the Send detour.

The receiving system object registers Cheat (0x1474d0d80), KickPlayer (0x1474d0ee0, registered at 0x1474cda34) and EasyAntiCheatPeerData (0x1474d0970, at 0x1474cd8b8) handlers. RVNG must filter these message types on the inject (receive) side as well as at the Send detour, so a peer can never route a KickPlayer or EAC-type message into the local game. These are the game's own call sites only; EAC itself was not analysed.

Sender callbacks pass a bogus shared_ptr {0x10, nullptr} to Send when allocation fails (e.g. 0x1474a8e49-0x1474a8e60). The original Send never dereferences it, so a full replacement must check ctl or ptr before calling msg->vf0.

The GameObject slot gate selects a set rather than enabling slots. Outer IsA ALiveGameObject with vf+0xaa0 (ALivePlayerPlane: 0x1416bb960, `mov al,1`) registers PhysicsOld, Physics and AirCurrentStates at 80 ms; otherwise AIPhysicsOld, AIPhysics and AIAirCurrentStates at 160 ms. Health (500 ms) and all handlers are registered in both cases (0x1474a7cda → 0x1474a7f83; 0x1474a7f7e jmp 0x1474a8219).

The Physics receive 0x1474aa1c0 copies the full incoming message, including +0x18/+0x19/+0x1c and the three arrays (0x1453ba0a0/0x1453ba030/0x1453b9fc0), into *(N+0x98) for any Outer. Only the cheat check depends on an ALivePlayerPlane Outer (IsA 0x147076d60 'LivePlayerPlane'). The other state-slot receivers (0x1474a9e70, 0x1474aa020, 0x1474aa540) copy msg+0x1c the same way.

The ElectronicMeasureEffect wrapper 0x147d60bc0 has no role==3 check, so a role-2 copy can emit outgoing EME messages. The other wrappers checked (LockedTarget at 0x147d608a7, EWF at 0x147d60cd4, EMF at 0x147d60b59) do check the role.

Identity on the wire comes from N+0x28 of the involved planes. SendDamage puts the attacker's +0xed0→+0x28 into Damage+0x20/+0x24 (0x1474a93d3-0x1474a9408); the EWF builder puts the target's +0xed0→+0x28 into WeaponData (0x147d60df3-0x147d60e19); and the prior digest's DM faction assigner 0x1471e0230 sorts on the same low dword. Both PCs must map player numbers to identical keys before the first Damage, fire or faction assignment.

The NM tick (0x1474ad5a0-0x1474ad615) also clears StrixManager+0x1f8 when SM+0x28 is set but the Strix client is null or client+0xe0 is 0. This flag was not mentioned in the report; leave it at 0 as well.

The GameModeState send callback 0x1474cdb90 and the Health send callback 0x1474a9250 restamp msg+0x8 with the synced clock. Physics, PhysicsOld and AirCurrentStates send the stored message without restamping. RTT (+0x28) is filled only when SM+0x1fa is set (0x1474cdc90).

In-game tests static RE cannot settle: (1) After registering the own plane's N offline, hook 0x14748d530 and the Send detour for 10 s and count Physics, AirCurrentStates and Health sends; expect about 125 Physics and few Health (Health's dirty setter is untraced). (2) Hook 0x1474efd50 offline to confirm the GI ticker reaches it every frame. (3) Set a data breakpoint on a copy's plane+0x8b1 during an online-mode respawn replay to find the game's setter. (4) Log whether PhaseState (SysObj+0x98) gets filled or flagged offline.

report.summary:
All addresses below are VAs in the 2026-11-02 AceCombat8.exe (551,201,904 bytes, base 0x140000000). Scratch evidence is in <scratchpad>/pvp_research/deep-server/.

1. **What the handlers say about the server.** I mapped every network class's handler table (regmap.txt). Read together, the handlers show that in a deathmatch Bandai's server extension does four things:
   - It routes damage reports to the room owner and relays the owner's results to everyone else.
   - It is the only score authority.
   - It owns the clock offset (RealTime) and the forced-end rule (PreparingMissionEnd addressed to each remaining member's own id).
   - It relays all the other gameplay messages, which the clients build themselves.

2. **Why the server scores, not the clients.** ALiveOnlineGameMode clears NetworkManager+0x739 at start (0x1471c5242). The score function 0x147d10f70 runs only when the client is offline, or when 0x739 is set and the client is host (0x147d10ea1-0x147d10ed4). So no deathmatch client ever computes a score or sends ScoreAddition. That function is the only sender of ScoreAddition (0x147d111f9). Scores therefore reach clients only as ScoreUpdate: an absolute {ScoreType, Score} list applied with SetScore +0xc18. The client still contains the whole formula: 0x147d11450, 0x147d1a4f0, 0x147d1a850, 0x147d19e90. The ScoreUpdate payload is pinned down; who computes it, and when it is sent, is inferred.

3. **Damage loop and the routing gap.** A DamageClient makes the room owner run AuthoritativeApply. A non-owner applies it only when Attribute bit 7 is set. A plain Damage message is always applied (ApplyDamageResult), so relays must never echo back to the sender.
   - The client gives the server nothing that separates the owner's own reports from its results, because both go through BroadcastDamage 0x147d1af10.
   - Bandai's exact routing is therefore stateful and cannot be seen from the client.
   - RVNG can tell the two apart by BroadcastDamage's return address: 0x147d103c3 for a report, 0x147d107fb for a result.

4. **Respawn is enforced on the client.**
   - On death, 0x147d56780 sets plane+0x3c2c and plane+0x3c2e and sends DestroyedLocation.
   - The plane tick 0x147d4ee80 counts RespawnTime 0x147d5d350 = mission-contents BaseRespawnTime (10) × the cost table's RespawnRate × the RespawnTime parts.
   - When the timer ends the client sends a header-only RespawnTimeEnd. Its client-side handler does nothing, so no reply is expected.
   - The owner's Respawn (location, rotation, RespawnCancel) is applied to copies through vf+0xbf8.
   - RequestRespawn, RequestTeleportToRespawnPoint and the rescue messages are not part of a normal deathmatch.

5. **Leaving.** The forced-end rule (ConnectionsLeftNum 1, MissionSuccessSeconds 105) appears to be server data: no InformationManager member holds the forced-end row type. The client force-terminates only when a PreparingMissionEnd arrives addressed to its own member id. A non-zero CoopResult or MatchResult gives Finished; zero gives Aborted.

6. **Messages RVNG does not need to send.** RealTime resets the synchronized clock offset. LatencyResponse, KickPlayer, ChangeBot and SetObjectInformation have no effect on the client: either no-op handlers or a stripped calculation. EvaluationList, MissionRewardUser and EventHash only fill NetworkManager or reward maps used outside combat.

7. **What this means for RVNG's stand-in.** Keep both PCs offline (StrixManager+0x1fa = 0, so every PC passes the host test). Then do three things:
   - **Damage:** pick one authority. Host-authoritative is the faithful choice; shooter-authoritative is simpler. Exchange BroadcastDamage results and apply them on the peer with ApplyDamageResult.
   - **Score:** make the host the single score authority by suppressing 0x147d10f70 on the client. The host then sends absolute ScoreUpdate equivalents, which the client applies with plane vf+0xc18.
   - **Respawn and end:** relay Respawn and DestroyedLocation. On link loss, call RecvPreparingMissionEnd (vf+0xdd0) locally.

The server's internals (routing state, the exact score rounding it uses, the result and reward flow) cannot be checked against official servers, and modded clients must not try.

findings.topic: Damage round trip: what the client requires
findings.finding:
**Shooter side.** TakeDamage branches at 0x147d1037d. When online and not (NM+0x739 and IsHost), it only reports: 0x147d103be calls BroadcastDamage(victim copy). In a deathmatch NM+0x739 is 0, because ALiveOnlineGameMode clears it at 0x1471c5242 (r12=0). So even the room owner reports. A crash (types 7/8/9) on your own plane pre-sets Killed and is also applied locally at 0x147d10401.

**BroadcastDamage 0x147d1af10.** It remaps WeaponId (+0x11) 0x68→0x1b and 0x69→0x1a. It reads IsHost at 0x147d1af7f and calls SendDamage 0x1474a9360(victim+0xed0, info, IsHost); IsHost becomes Attribute bit 7.

**Receive side.**
- Damage handler 0x1474aa990 calls ApplyNetworkDamage 0x1474aacb0 with flag 0. That always ends in ApplyDamageResult 0x147d1b070 (call at 0x1474ab045). There is no role check and no host check, and the target is N+0x20.
- DamageClient handler 0x1474aaae0 copies only +0x10/+0x14 and +0x20..+0x31 into a new Damage (ctor 0x1474bbec0). It drops TriggerTime, Health and ElectronicMeasureData, then calls ApplyNetworkDamage with flag 1.
- With flag 1: if IsHost (0x1474aaf05), AuthoritativeApply 0x147d104a0 runs at 0x1474aaf6f. It clamps, sets Killed, applies, chains children and parent, and re-broadcasts the result through BroadcastDamage at 0x147d107f6. Otherwise ApplyDamageResult runs only if Attribute bit 7 is set (0x1474aaf79 cmp [rsp+0x21],0 / jge).
- The attacker is resolved through StrixManager+0x2e0 (0x1474bbfe0). The cheat check 0x1474a3cb0 does not block.
sources: deep-server/b1.txt xrefs: BroadcastDamage callers 0x147d103be(0x147d102ba) and 0x147d107f6(0x147d10738); ApplyNetDamage callers 0x1474aaa54, 0x1474aabfd

findings.topic: Damage round trip: the server rule the client forces (DamageClient recipients, echo, Health)
findings.finding:
**Who must receive DamageClient: only the room owner (the host-test machine).** Non-owners ignore it unless bit 7 is set. With bit 7 set (a report from the owner), a non-owner would apply it unclamped as a final result, and the owner's own copy would never be damaged.

**The result must not echo to its sender.** The owner has already applied it in AuthoritativeApply, and the Damage handler applies again with no guard. ApplyDamageResult is a no-op only on a dead victim, so echoing a lethal result is harmless but a non-lethal one is not. Rule: relay the owner's Damage results to every member except the owner.

**The ambiguity the server must solve.** In a deathmatch the owner's own hits arrive as Damage with bit 7, and so do its results. Both come from BroadcastDamage with identical fields: +0x34 is never filled by clients, and Attribute is rebuilt from info+0x21..0x24 plus IsHost. So the real server must keep state, for example by pairing each DamageClient it sends with the owner's next matching result (target, attacker, weapon, type). That is unknowable from the client.

**Damage.Health +0x34.** Never written or read by the client. It is server-side or unused. Send 0.

**How RVNG tells reports from results.** RVNG controls both ends, so it can classify by BroadcastDamage's return address: 0x147d103c3 is a report from TakeDamage; 0x147d107fb is a result from the AuthoritativeApply tail.
sources: derived from the handler logic above (0x1474aaef4-0x1474ab045) and from the two BroadcastDamage call sites (b1.txt)

findings.topic: Score authority online: who computes deathmatch scores
findings.finding:
**The gate.** The score function 0x147d10f70(victim, dmg xmm1, attacker r8, weapon r9b, indirect [rsp+0x20]) is called from ApplyHealthDamage's tail only when !(StrixManager+0x1fa) || (NM+0x739 && IsHost) (0x147d10ea1-0x147d10ed4). NM+0x739 is set only by the campaign mode and is cleared in online modes, so no deathmatch client runs it.

**ScoreAddition is never sent in a deathmatch.** Its only sender, SendScoreAddition 0x1474a9c70, is inside that function (0x147d111f9). The function sends through the attacker's ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane (class 0x146ef9b60) and then calls attacker vf+0xc10 AddScore.
- Two more, unguarded callers of 0x147d10f70 exist: 0x147e8f892 and 0x147e8f913. These are lambdas that pass damage 0 and an attacker weak pointer at obj+0x484. Their purpose is unknown; probably NPC destruction credit.

**ScoreUpdate is the only way scores reach clients.** It is factory-only (vtable 0x14bfd7bb0 has one reference, 0x1452b2c9e).
- ScoreUpdate handler 0x1474abca0 builds TArray<{u8 type, int value}> and calls the target plane's vf+0xc18 SetScore (0x1474abe1c). There is no role check, and the target is the object with that network id.
- SetScore base 0x147d19390 replaces map +0xe08[type] with float(value). Type 15 (ThreatLevelPoint) instead accumulates into +0xe00. A non-zero value triggers popup 0x147d198a0, and the function then calls AuthorityGameMode (world+0x158) vf+0xc18 to re-sort ScoreRankList.
- The player-plane override 0x147d5dc00 computes total and assist deltas and feeds the HUD (0x147d5e220) and Evaluation (+0x16c8). An absolute update equal to the local value therefore produces no popup.
- ScoreAddition handler 0x1474aba20 calls vf+0xc10 AddScore (increment). It can redirect to another object through 0x1474bbf90 / +0x53c8 / 0x1471d16e0(+0x108).

findings.topic: Deathmatch score formula (the function the server must reproduce)
findings.finding:
The calculator is 0x147d11450(victim, out map, dmg, attacker, weapon, indirect). It reads per-mode switches through 0x1471b57b0(obj, ELiveScoreType index). The rates come from InformationManager ScoreRateTable_: PlayerKill +0xcb8, PlayerDamage +0xcbc, KillAssist +0xcc4, IndirectKill +0xcd8 (NpcDamage +0xcb4, Boss +0xcc0 for other modes).

**Base(victim, attacker)** is computed by 0x147d1a4f0 as int( BaseScore(victim+0xfdc PlaneCost) [0x147351130] × CostDiffRate(attacker+0xfdc − victim+0xfdc) [0x147351530] × rank correction × team rank × threat ). The individual factors:
- **Rank correction:** only if switch 16 (bCalcOverallScoreRank) is on and the victim's total score is above 0. It is looked up by player count and rank (0x147d199b0, map at mgr+0xe28).
- **Team rank:** switch 17; off in a deathmatch.
- **Threat:** 0x147d19e90; it is 1.0 unless switch 15 (ThreatLevelPoint) is on.

**Per damage result, when the victim is a player plane and the hit is not indirect (switch 2):**
PlayerDamageScore = int(Base × dmg / victim MaxHealth(+0x3b4) × PlayerDamageScoreRate + 0.5).

**When the victim dies (vf+0xc30 false) (switch 3):** KillBase = int(Base × PlayerKillScoreRate) (0x147d1a850). The type is 3 PlayerKillScore, or 13 IndirectKillScore with value int(KillBase × IndirectKillBonusRate) when the indirect flag is set.

**Deathmatch table values:**
- only switches 2, 3, 13 and 16 are on;
- all three rates 1.0; CostDiffRate 1.0 for every cost difference;
- 2-player rank correction [1.0, 1.0];
- BaseScore 1400 at cost 0 up to 4000 at cost 4800.

In 1v1 a kill from full health therefore pays the killer about 2 × BaseScore(victim cost): the damage share plus the kill. VictoryScore 500000 is unreachable, so a deathmatch ends on time-up.
sources: deep-server/scorecalc.txt (0x147d11450-0x147d120fd: switch indices at 0x147d1149f/0x147d1160a/0x147d11841/0x147d11905…, multiplies at 0x147d1167e-0x147d1169c, 0x147d118a8-0x147d118de)

table values: prior verified finding 'Score rules' in tasks/we9cc770a.output (dt.py on DT_ScoreConstTable, DT_PlayerAircraftCost, DT_PlayerAircraftCostDifferenceRate, DT_SoloRankCorrectionScoreRateTable)

findings.topic: SetObjectInformation: the client ignores it, but it carries the server's scoring inputs
findings.finding:
SetObjectInformation is registered on the System object, but its handler 0x145203500 only releases the TSharedPtr: it is a no-op. The class vtable 0x14bfd73b0 has one code reference, the factory 0x1452b5697.

Its fields (OwnersNetworkId, MaxHealth, PlaneCost, Score, Faction, Parent, DamageRateToParent, Category) are exactly the inputs of the client's damage and score code (MaxHealth +0x3b4, PlaneCost +0xfdc, Faction +0x3b2, parent +0x518 / DamageRateToParent +0xcbc). That supports the reading that the server keeps its own object table and runs the same formula.

It is not proven which side sends it: senders built inside obfuscated .sbss code would not show up in a RIP-relative scan. RVNG never needs to send it.

findings.topic: Respawn: timing is enforced on the client; the server only receives RespawnTimeEnd
findings.finding:
**Death.** The player-plane death function 0x147d56780 sets +0x3c2c=1 (respawn timer) and +0x3c2e=1 (downed). It then calls 0x147d61450, which sends DestroyedLocation (0x1474c6250) when the plane's role is 3.

**Timer.** The plane tick 0x147d4ee80 adds dt to +0x3c28. When that reaches RespawnTime(0x147d5d350), it clamps, clears +0x3c2c and calls 0x147d5d950. That clears +0x3c2e and, for a role-3 plane, sends RespawnTimeEnd (0x1474c6530 at 0x147d5d984). The message is header only, addressed to the sender's own plane.

**RespawnTime(0x147d5d350)** = RespawnRate(InfoMgr 0x147351330, PlaneCost +0xfdc) × mission-contents row for the mode (0x147353820(InfoMgr, mode type)) +0xb0 BaseRespawnTime (10) × the plane's parts parameter 0x34c (RespawnTime) × the product of parts parameter 0x34d (RespawnTime_Team) over same-faction planes. RespawnRate runs from 0.4 at cost 0 to 2.0 at cost 4400 (prior table dump).

**Receive side.**
- The RespawnTimeEnd handler 0x1474c89d0 does nothing: no reply is expected.
- The pilot then respawns locally (pause-menu point picker 0x1475d4b70 → plane +0xbf0 → RespawnAt 0x147d18c80, which sends Respawn through 0x1474a98e0 with no role check).
- Peers' Respawn handler 0x1474ab4f0 calls vf+0xbf8(location, rotation, RespawnCancel) with no role check. An echo to the owner would therefore respawn it twice.
- The DestroyedLocation handler 0x1474c8430 applies to role-2 copies only: SetActorLocation 0x143fd2150, then +0x3c2e=1.

**Spawn protection.** 0x147d187f0, called after every respawn or teleport including on copies (0x147d5d040), sets obj+0xdfc=1; CanTakeDamage refuses non-crash damage while it is set (0x147d12a01). It also adds {network key, now + 0x2faf080 ticks = 5 s} to 0x147ec9820(world)+0x818. Firing clears +0xdfc (0x147d61f2f).
sources: deep-server/b1.txt, b2.txt (xrefs: SendRespawnTimeEnd only 0x147d5d984; RescueDone callers 0x1474c8942, 0x147d4ef41, 0x147d5d561)

findings.topic: RequestRespawn, RequestTeleportToRespawnPoint, TeleportToRespawnPoint and the rescue messages
findings.finding:
**RequestRespawn** (factory-only) handler 0x1474ab380 acts only on role-2 copies (vf+0xc48). It calls RespawnAt(copy, PlayerStartNetworkId, RespawnCancel), which itself sends a Respawn through the copy's network object and runs vf+0xbf8. It can force a copy, and through the re-sent Respawn its owner, to a start point. It is not part of the normal deathmatch flow (inferred).

**RequestTeleportToRespawnPoint** (factory-only) handler 0x1474ab6c0 acts only on role 2 and calls 0x147d18e20(copy, id, send=0).

**TeleportToRespawnPoint** (client-built) handler 0x1474ab830 acts only on role 3 (your own plane), calling vf+0xc00. Relaying a peer's teleport to others therefore does nothing; it is information for the server or a correction sent to the owner.

**Placement needs no network.** The online TeleportPlayers state 0x1471c6c90 places every player and AI plane on every PC with 0x147d18e20(plane, 0x147391240(world mgr, 0, plane), send=1) followed by protection 0x147d187f0. Only your own plane's teleport is sent.

**Rescue is allies only.** RespawnRescueTry is sent by 0x147d5d710 only for same-faction planes (0x147390f80 by +0x3b2) inside radius +0x3c34, and only when gate 0x147ec94e0(world) is on. Every deathmatch pilot has its own faction, so RespawnRescueTry and RespawnRescueResult never occur in a deathmatch.

findings.topic: Kill credit and the indirect-kill window
findings.finding:
The window is NM+0x740 = GetIntSetting(InfoMgr, 'INDIRECT_KILL_VALID_TIME_SEC' (string 0x14cb67c40), default 0x1e = 30) × 1e7 ticks, set at 0x1474ad549 by 0x1474ad130.
- 0x1474ad130's only caller is 0x1474b6de7. That call comes after the online-only block (0x1474b6c55 je 0x1474b6cf2), so within that function it is unconditional.
- Whether the whole network-manager setup function runs offline is not proven here.

The last-player-attacker record +0x498 is written only while switch 13 is on (prior verified). In an online deathmatch no client scores, so the server must apply the same rule itself (inferred): when a victim's own PC reports a crash death (DamageType 7/8/9, Killed=1, no player attacker), credit IndirectKillScore to the last player who damaged that victim within INDIRECT_KILL_VALID_TIME_SEC. The server can know 'last damager' from the Damage results it relays.

findings.topic: Leaving and forced end: PreparingMissionEnd
findings.finding:
**Sending.** PreparingMissionEnd is client-built: sender 0x1474c69c0, called only from PrepMEndSync 0x1471cb5e0, which is in turn called from GameTerminating 0x1471c8269, OnGameFinish 0x1471c97bd and RecvPreparingMissionEnd 0x1471cb8ee. It is sent through the local plane's network object, so msg+0x14 is the sender's own plane id (= member id).

**Receiving.** The handler 0x1474c8e10 calls GameMode vf+0xdd0 = RecvPreparingMissionEnd 0x1471cb7e0(msg+0x14, CoopResult, MatchResult):
- local id = online ? Strix member id (0x1474efb30(NM+0x520)) : 0;
- PrepMEndSync always runs, with the message's flags when the id is not local;
- only when msg+0x14 equals the local id and the match is not finished: ForcedTerminationState +0x804 = 2 (Finished) if CoopResult or MatchResult is non-zero, else 1 (Aborted); +0x808=1; notice 0x147243560; finish reason +0x538 = 4; OnGameFinish +0xab8.

A member's own PreparingMissionEnd never comes back to it unless someone readdresses it. So forced termination is driven by a server-made PreparingMissionEnd {type 2, NetworkId = recipient member, MatchResult/CoopResult}.

**The rule is server data.** FLiveMissionForcedEndRuleDataTableRow {ModeType, ConnectionsLeftNum, DifferenceTeamsPlanesNum, TeamsPlanesLeftNum, MissionSuccessSeconds} is not held by any LiveInformationManager map, and none of the 26 mission-contents row readers I sampled reads those fields. Inferred server rule: when the remaining member count is ≤ ConnectionsLeftNum (1), send each remaining member a PreparingMissionEnd addressed to itself, with MatchResult non-zero if elapsed play ≥ MissionSuccessSeconds (105 s), else zero.

**Timeouts.** Online, the network-manager tick lowers NM+0x624 (PREPARING_MISSION_END_TIMEOUT_SEC, default 0x1e, set at 0x1471cb77f) and sets stage 3 at 0x1474b9c4b, which blocks GameTerminating. Stage 2 is set only by callbacks 0x1471d47c0 and 0x1471d4750 (functor vtable 0x14cb37658, installed by 0x1471cbeb0 around a UI call 0x14793ead0).

findings.topic: KickPlayer (part of the game's own cheat-report path; keep it unreached)
findings.finding:
KickPlayer {TargetNetworkId} is client-built. The sender 0x1474cee50 has one caller, 0x1474a3800, inside 0x1474a3430: the game's own aggregator of FLiveMessageCheat reports.
- It sends a kick request for a reported member once enough distinct reporters agree on cheat type 1, when online and the network manager's 0x1474b3860 check passes.
- The client-side KickPlayer handler 0x1474d0ee0 is a no-op.
- The kick itself happens in Strix: ULiveNetworkManager has reflected KickRoomMemberSuccess/Failed callbacks, and ELiveForceDisconnectType has KickRoomMember.

Offline the send is dropped (Strix context null), and RVNG should never construct one.

findings.topic: Time messages: RealTime, LatencyCheck/LatencyResponse, GameTime, TimeUp, PauseTime
findings.finding:
**RealTime** (factory-only), handler 0x1474d00c0: if a game mode exists and RealTime ≠ 0, it sets the synchronized-clock offset singleton(0x147907550)+0x20 = RealTime − (QPC(0x147907660) + [s+0x18] − [s+0x8]). Synchronized now then equals the server's time, in 100 ns ticks. No latency compensation happens on the client.

**LatencyCheck {SenderMemberId}** is sent periodically from the network-manager tick (0x1474adeeb → 0x1474ceb60). Its handler does nothing.

**LatencyResponse** (factory-only), handler 0x1474d0bf0: when SenderMemberId equals the local id it only reads the clock; the shipping build stores nothing. Round-trip time reaches the member table through GameModeState.RoundTripTime (0x1474ba1f0).

**GameTime** (host-built, bSetByHost), handler 0x1474cff60: calls GameMode vf+0xa58(BeginningTime, 1) and 0x1471b8290(gm, Beginning, PhaseBeginning, Finish, 1).

**TimeUp** (host-built, sender 0x1474ce590 from +0xb30 at 0x1471c938b), handler 0x1474d0370: gm+0x4d0[Phase] = SendTime, then gm vf+0xb30.

**PauseTime**, handler 0x1474d0220: calls gm vf+0xaa0.

The server only relays GameTime, TimeUp and PauseTime. RealTime and LatencyResponse are its own.

findings.topic: End-of-match data: EvaluationData, EvaluationList, ResultState, MissionRewardUser, EventHash, Error, bots
findings.finding:
**Evaluation and result:**
- **EvaluationData** is client-built (sender 0x1474ce080 from the OnGameFinish chunk 0x1471c96e7). Handler 0x1474cf3c0 stores the sender's state in NM+0x90 (0x1474bc720) and writes the sender plane's evaluation counters (+0x1764..+0x179x). The server relays it.
- **EvaluationList** (factory-only), handler 0x1474cf670: rebuilds a map from EvaluationUsersList (element stride 0x28) into NM+0xe0 (0x146e3a8e0). These are server-assigned evaluation titles (ELiveEvaluationType); the consumer is likely the result screen (not traced).
- **ResultState** is client-built (from the result screen 0x1480f3fac). Handler 0x1474cfe00 → NM+0x2b0.
- **MissionRewardUser** (factory-only, Chronicle rewards), handler 0x1474c8f80 → manager 0x147ece300(world)+0xc20.

**Other factory-only messages:**
- **EventHash**, handler 0x1474d06c0 → NM 0x1474b68d0: adds EventHash to NM+0x180[PackageHash] and broadcasts NM+0x1d0. EP_DM is radio-only, so not needed in a deathmatch (inferred).
- **Error**, handled by NM 0x1474b9080, the session-error path (also the router fallback at 0x1474efa4c).
- **ChangeBot**, handler 0x1474d13c0: no-op.
- **OperateBot**, handler 0x1474d1500 → AI bot manager 0x147494da0, only when online. The deathmatch row has AllowBot=false.
- NpcRandomLotteryResult, ALCMLottery, StaurosLottery, PVPVE*, AI*, lobby, guild, centurion and avatar types belong to other modes.

**RVNG needs none of these during combat.** Whether the Result map waits for EvaluationList or MissionRewardUser is unknown.
sources: deep-server/b1.txt, b2.txt (EvalData sender xref 0x1471c96e7; ResultState sender 0x1480f3fac)

findings.topic: Caveat: 'factory-only' is strong evidence but not proof that a message is server-made
findings.finding:
The 47 'factory-only' types were found with a RIP-relative lea/mov/call scan of executable sections. That scan does find plain references inside .sbss: for example the SystemObject constructor 0x15c1a05f0 using the GameModeState vtable. It cannot see message construction in obfuscated protected code.

For DamageClient, ScoreUpdate, RequestRespawn, RequestTeleportToRespawnPoint, RealTime, LatencyResponse, EvaluationList, EventHash and SetObjectInformation, I confirmed again on this build that the vtable has exactly one code reference: its factory.

The handler semantics above hold either way. Only 'who sends' is inferred.

rvngImplications: **Keep both PCs offline** (StrixManager_ +0x1fa = 0, GameInstance+0x910) so every PC passes the host test 0x1474b38d0 and no Strix send ever leaves (0x1474a2190 returns while 0x14e4c5818 is null). RVNG's link replaces the server. Never construct KickPlayer, Cheat, LatencyCheck or EasyAntiCheatPeerData equivalents, and keep the game's own cheat-vote path 0x1474a3430 unreached.

**Damage, faithful 'room owner' model.**
- On the client PC, detour AuthoritativeApply 0x147d104a0. When the return address is 0x147d103e6 (TakeDamage's local branch) and the victim is the role-2 copy (vf+0xc48), do not apply locally: serialize the info struct as a DamageClient (Damage fields +0x20..+0x31) and send it to the host.
- On the host, rebuild the info the way ApplyNetworkDamage 0x1474aacb0 does (attacker = the host's copy of the client plane, the explicit pointer, because StrixManager+0x2e0 is empty offline) and call 0x147d104a0(host own plane, info).
- Capture every BroadcastDamage 0x147d1af10 call whose return address is 0x147d107fb (a result) and send it to the peer, which calls ApplyDamageResult 0x147d1b070(target, info) on the matching object.
- Never echo a result back to the PC that produced it.
- The simpler alternative is shooter-authoritative: no client detour; both PCs exchange results captured at 0x147d107fb.

**Score, faithful model.**
- On the client, detour the score function 0x147d10f70 to return, which emulates the online non-host gate at 0x147d10ea1.
- On the host, let it run natively (offline gate passes). After each host ApplyHealthDamage, read the scoring plane's score map (+0xe08, types 2, 3 and 13) and send a ScoreUpdate equivalent {plane id, [(type, absolute int)]}.
- On the receiving PC, call that plane's vf+0xc18 SetScore with a TArray<{u8 type; int32 value}>, which is what the native ScoreUpdate handler 0x1474abca0 does. SetScore also re-sorts the ranking (world+0x158 vf+0xc18) and drives the HUD popup through the deltas computed in the player-plane override 0x147d5dc00.
- If both PCs keep scoring natively instead, send ScoreUpdate anyway as a periodic drift correction (absolute values give zero deltas when they already agree).

**Respawn, natively.**
- Let each pilot's own timer (0x147d4ee80/0x147d5d350) and the pause respawn UI (0x1475d4b70 → +0xbf0) run.
- Hook RespawnAt 0x147d18c80 or vf+0xbf8 on your own plane and send {location, rotation, RespawnCancel}. The peer calls copy vf+0xbf8(location, rotation, RespawnCancel), which is what Respawn handler 0x1474ab4f0 does.
- Forward DestroyedLocation the same way: the peer calls SetActorLocation on the copy and sets copy+0x3c2e=1, as handler 0x1474c8430 does.
- RespawnTimeEnd needs no reply. The host may use it only to validate the following Respawn.
- Do not send RequestRespawn or RequestTeleportToRespawnPoint. TeleportPlayers (0x1471c6c90) already places both planes on each PC, provided both PCs agree on the plane order and factions.

**Kill credit.** Let the native Killed flag and ApplyHealthDamage paths kill and credit. For crash deaths, forward the victim's own Killed=1 crash result (type 7/8/9). The host's score function then credits IndirectKillScore through +0x498 inside NM+0x740. Read NM+0x740 in game to learn the live INDIRECT_KILL_VALID_TIME_SEC (default 30 s).

**Leaving.**
- On link loss (heartbeat timeout), call the surviving PC's game mode vf+0xdd0 = RecvPreparingMissionEnd 0x1471cb7e0(gm, memberId=0, CoopResult=0, MatchResult = (elapsed since BeginningTime ≥ 105 s) ? 1 : 0). Offline the local member id is 0, so this forces ForcedTermination (finish reason +0x538 = 4) with Finished or Aborted, exactly as a server-made PreparingMissionEnd would.
- During a normal end, relay each PC's own PreparingMissionEnd {CoopResult, MatchResult} to the peer by calling its vf+0xdd0 with the peer's id (any non-zero id other than 0) so the PreparingMissionEnd sync stages advance.

**Clock.** At match start (and optionally every few seconds) the host sends its synchronized now (0x147907550/0x147907660 base + [s+0x20]). The client writes singleton(0x147907550)+0x20 = hostNow + RTT/2 − (QPC + [s+0x18] − [s+0x8]), which is what the RealTime handler 0x1474d00c0 does. Then forward the host's GameTime (call gm vf+0xa58 and 0x1471b8290 as handler 0x1474cff60 does) so FinishTime agrees on both PCs.

**Ignore entirely in a deathmatch:** SetObjectInformation (no-op handler), LatencyResponse, EvaluationList, MissionRewardUser, EventHash, ChangeBot, OperateBot, NpcRandomLotteryResult, PVPVE*, AI*, RespawnRescueTry/Result and TeleportToRespawnPoint. Health, GameModeState, IGCState and ResultState are peer relays that the deep-sync design owns.
blockers: **Bandai's real damage routing cannot be recovered.** The owner's reports and its authoritative results are indistinguishable on the wire: same message, same fields, Attribute bit 7 set in both. Health +0x34 is never filled by clients. So the official server must keep state. Exactly how it pairs a DamageClient with its result, and how it treats the owner's reports, cannot be recovered from the client and cannot be tested without contacting official servers.

**The server's score code is not in the exe.** That the official server uses the same formula as 0x147d11450, the same rounding, sends ScoreUpdate after every result, and addresses it only to the scorer's plane is all inferred.
**The sender of SetObjectInformation, EventHash and EvaluationList is unproven.** Message construction inside obfuscated .sbss code would not show up in the RIP-relative scan.

**Result-screen dependency is unknown.** Whether the Result map (reached through OnGameFinish → Ended → +0xb18) waits for EvaluationList or MissionRewardUser, or is gated by NetworkResultManager, is unknown.

**PreparingMissionEnd stage 2 is not fully traced.** It comes from UI callbacks (0x1471d47c0/0x1471d4750 installed by 0x1471cbeb0). If that callback never fires offline, GameTerminating stalls whatever RVNG relays (deep-sync area).
**Every VA here is specific to this build.** All addresses belong to the 2026-11-02 exe, and RVNG must find them by signature.
openQuestions: **Score parity (solo, offline deathmatch, mission 1600x0).** Hook 0x147d11450's out-map and 0x147d10f70. Damage a role-2 copy to death with missiles. Log each (type, value), the victim's PlaneCost +0xfdc and MaxHealth +0x3b4, and Base from 0x147d1a4f0. Check that the damage shares plus the kill add up to about 2 × BaseScore(victim cost), and that the 2-player rank correction is 1.0.

**ScoreUpdate injection.** On a copy, call vf+0xc18 with [(3, 5000)]. Check that the ranking HUD (DeathMatchExInfo) updates, that RankChanged fires, and that a second identical SetScore produces no popup (zero delta).

**Report/result classification.** With RVNG's BroadcastDamage hook, log its return address for (a) your hit on the copy offline: expect 0x147d107fb; (b) a crash of your own plane: expect 0x147d107fb, with Killed=1 and type 7/8/9.

**Respawn timing.** After dying, log +0x3c28 and +0x3c2c every 100 ms and the moment 0x1474c6530 is called. Compare with 10 × RespawnRate(cost) × parts. Check whether the respawn point picker becomes usable only after +0x3c2c clears, and whether AutomaticRespawnTime then auto-calls +0xbf0.

**Forced end.** Mid-match, call vf+0xdd0(gm, 0, 0, 0) once before 105 s and once after with MatchResult=1. Verify +0x804 = 1 (Aborted) or 2 (Finished), +0x538 = 4, the notice dialog appears, stage +0x80c reaches 2 when the notice closes, and the state machine reaches Ended (or the abort path 0x1471c5f70).
**Clock sync.** On two PCs, write singleton(0x147907550)+0x20 from the host's value. Then compare GamePlaying's remaining time (+0xa88) on both PCs over 210 s; drift should be under one frame.
**Indirect-kill window.** In an offline deathmatch, read NM (GI+0x928)+0x740 after load. 300,000,000 means 30 s; 0 means 0x1474ad130 never ran offline, in which case write it yourself.
**Unguarded score callers.** Hook the lambdas 0x147e8f860 and 0x147e8f8e0 during a deathmatch to confirm they never fire for player planes (they would score outside the online gate).

**Result screen.** Let an offline deathmatch time out with the +0xb18 travel enabled. Watch whether /Game/OnlineMode/Maps/Menu/Result loads, and whether it waits on NM+0xe0 (EvaluationList) or the reward manager 0x147ece300(world)+0xc20.
