missed: End-of-match blocker (static, 2026-11-02 build). PreparingMissionEnd stage 2 (gm+0x80c=2), which GameTerminating 0x1471c8190 needs for every non-Aborted end, is written only at the end of a callback chain that starts in the handler of the server-made MissionRewardUser message. The chain: MissionRewardUser handler 0x1474c8f80 (chunk 0x1474c900c) checks the AuthorityGameMode is ALiveOnlineGameMode, stage < 2 and NM+0x3b8 > 1, then installs functor vtable 0x14cb375f0 (at 0x1474c964d). Its callback 0x1471d4ab0 calls 0x1471cbbb0, which goes to UserDataManager (GI+0x8e0)+0x10f0 and starts async op 0x1479b5da0 with functor 0x14cb376c0. That functor's callback 0x1471d4900 calls 0x1471cbeb0, which runs UI call 0x14793ead0 with functor 0x14cb37658, whose callbacks 0x1471d47c0 and 0x1471d4750 write stage 2. The handler always calls 0x1471cbb20(gm,1) as well. A dword-write scan of +0x80c finds no other writer of 2. Consequence offline: a Timeup or VictoryScore end stalls in GameTerminating at stage 1 forever, because the PREPARING_MISSION_END timeout runs only when +0x1fa is set (0x1474b9c07). RVNG must write gm+0x80c=2 itself, the same way 0x1471d47c4 does. Test: let an offline DM time out, log +0x80c and +0x804 every second, and check that the state machine stays in GameTerminating until RVNG writes 2.

A forced end reported as Finished (+0x804=2, MatchResult or CoopResult non-zero) also needs stage >= 2 (GameTerminating 0x1471c8280-0x1471c8290). The forced-termination notice functor 0x14cb37790, installed at 0x1471cba1b, only clears +0x808 (callbacks 0x1471d4600 and 0x1471d4610). Only Aborted (+0x804=1) proceeds without stage 2. GameTerminating's own PrepMEndSync call (0x1471c8269) needs 0x1474b3860, which requires the Strix client global 0x14e4c5818, so it never runs offline. Mode types 10 and 11 (OnlineTutorials and OnlineFreeFlight) bypass the stage gate at 0x1471c81fc.

Spawn-protection expiry has an offline risk (static; the outcome is inferred). Entries in ALiveOnlineGameMode+0x818 are keyed by [plane+0xed0]+0x28, the network object id. Offline no plane has a network object, so every key is 0, and 0x147d18873 reuses the single key-0 entry. The expiry function 0x1471cfdc0, called from the online-game-mode tick at 0x1471c7ebb, clears +0xdfc only on the first plane in the world-manager list (+0x138) whose key matches, then stops (0x1471cfe67-0x1471cfe77). It also clears every key-0 object in the category-0xf list (0x1471cfed3-0x1471cfede). The opponent copy gets +0xdfc=1 on every vf+0xbf8 respawn (0x147d5d040). Its own fire path (0x147d61f2f in 0x147d61853) may not run on a copy, so the copy can stay immune to every damage type except 7. Test: after the opponent copy respawns offline, read copy+0xdfc every second for 10 s.

Native class getters identified by their name strings: 0x146ef8de0 ULiveNetworkManager, 0x146ef9b60 ULiveNetworkPlayerPlane, 0x146dd41c0 ALiveOnlineGameMode, 0x146d0dee0 ALiveGameObject, 0x147076d60 ALivePlayerPlane, 0x146dcdcf0 ALiveGameMode. So 0x147ec9710 returns the AuthorityGameMode as ALiveGameMode, and 0x147ec9820 returns it as ALiveOnlineGameMode. The spawn-protection list and the PreparingMissionEnd target therefore exist only under online-derived game modes, which includes the deathmatch mode offline.

Score map layout for RVNG's host-side reader: plane+0xe08 is a TMap<uint8 type, float value> with 16-byte elements (key byte +0, float +4, hash-next int +8, read at 0x147d19430-0x147d1943f and 0x147d195d0-0x147d195e9). Hash buckets are at +0xe40/+0xe48 and the bucket count at +0xe50. A ScoreUpdate-equivalent passed to vf+0xc18 must be a TArray of 8-byte {u8 type; pad[3]; int32 value} elements (0x1474abdb0-0x1474abdf0).

ObjectAttach is another host-built client message, which the server only relays. 0x147d1afd0 (12 callers) sends it through 0x1474a9740 (vtable 0x14bfd7090) only when IsHost is true and a network object exists (0x147d1b03d). Offline the send is dropped.

The game's own cheat-report and anti-cheat call sites to keep unreached (listed only, not analysed). The cheat check 0x1474a3cb0 runs inside ApplyNetworkDamage (0x1474aaeef). NM cheat report 0x1474b8bb0 has 9 callers, including the PlayerPlane weapon-fire handlers (0x1474c75cc in 0x1474c73f0, 0x1474c78a7 in 0x1474c76c0, 0x1474c7b8c in 0x1474c79b0) and 0x147d5b6cf. The Cheat receive path runs 0x1474d0d80, 0x1474b8de0 and 0x1474a3430, which ends in KickPlayer. The EasyAntiCheatPeerData sender sits at 0x1474ce9e7 (vtable 0x14bfd7310; seam-verify/msg_vt_users.txt). If RVNG feeds remote fire or damage through the native message handlers rather than calling the apply functions directly, these report paths run. Offline they drop at the Strix send.

Clock reset: 0x1474b3930, called only from 0x1474b8515 in 0x1474b8478, sets singleton(0x147907550)+0x8 and +0x10 to QPC. It sets +0x18 to a Strix base from 0x14528cb50 using NM+0x520 (0 when there is no Strix client) and +0x20 to 0. This can wipe an offset RVNG injected.

TimeUp is sent only by the host: vf+0xb30 0x1471c92f0 calls vf+0xb80 (not finished), then IsHost 0x1471c9325, then +0x1fa, then NM+0x4c0, before sending at 0x1471c938b. LatencyCheck goes out every 60 s (0x23c34600 ticks, 0x1474ade5c), online only, through NM+0x4c0.

The respawn function vf+0xbf0 0x147d5ccd0 itself clears the respawn timer (+0x3c2c=0 at 0x147d5cd3d, +0x3c28=0 at 0x147d5cd44) and applies protection twice: through RespawnAt, then vf+0xbf8 (0x147d5d040), then directly at 0x147d5cd15. The plane code does not require the timer to have ended before a respawn; only the UI enforces that.

The online setup that clears NM+0x739 (0x1471c5180) is game-mode vfunc +0x9f8 in the DM, Online and SoloPVP vtables (0x14c693718, 0x14c980e98, 0x14ca32fe8). GameTerminating is state slot +0xd50 (0x1471c8190) and vf+0xb30 is 0x1471c92f0 in all three vtables.
